desc: A talisman depicting the exultation of the aging untouchable, whose head resembles a sprig of ripe grapes. Raises attack power when madness is triggered in the vicinity. "Gift your madness to our Lord. Bless our brethren with grapes. Take care that they fully ripen."
location: Guaranteed Drop: Abyssal Woods Aged One's Exultation is dropped by the Aging Untouchable found nearest to the Abandoned Church in the Abyssal Woods. The Aging Untouchable is only vulnerable after it has been parried.
whatItIs: A talisman that turns nearby madness into raw power. When madness is triggered in the vicinity, attack power goes up.
whyItMatters: It rewards builds that can bring madness into the area, and does nothing at all for characters who never trigger it. That makes it a niche pick, best saved for a build with a clear path to the condition.
whenToUse: Equip it in a slot once the build can reliably trigger madness, since it is idle until then. The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is required, and the talisman is a guaranteed drop from the Aging Untouchable found nearest to the Abandoned Church in the Abyssal Woods, vulnerable only after a parry.
name: Aged One's Exultation
effect: Madness in the vicinity increases attack power

desc: A talisman depicting a soul taken by sickness. When certain ailments are triggered, this talisman grants resistance to the same ailment. When the weak were infected with the dreaded fly sickness, they perished well before the metamorphosis could take hold. Oddly, those who cared for the infected and made certain they were given a proper burial were never afflicted themselves.
location: Ailment Talisman is found in the Gravesite Plain at the Abandoned Ailing Village. It is located on a corpse at the edge of an unfinished wooden bridge.
whatItIs: When certain ailments trigger, resistance to that same ailment arrives with the hit. It is reactive rather than a blanket immunity, so the protection shows up around the moment a status lands.
whyItMatters: It softens the moments when an ailment would otherwise punish the character with its full effect. The resistance matches the ailment that fires, so a fight mixing several different statuses still needs separate coverage.
whenToUse: Equip it against enemies whose moves set up repeated ailment triggers. The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion brings it; it waits on a corpse at the edge of an unfinished wooden bridge in the Abandoned Ailing Village, Gravesite Plain.
name: Ailment Talisman

desc: Item cut from the horns of the Regal Ancestor Spirit. Restore FP upon defeating enemies. A number of new growths bud from the antler-like horns of the fallen king, each glowing with light. Thus does new life grow from death, and from death, one obtains power.
location: Trade the Remembrance of the Regal Ancestor, gained by defeating Regal Ancestor Spirit, with Finger Reader Enia. Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).
whatItIs: Horn trimmings from a great stag, worn in the talisman slot. Every enemy defeated restores some FP, so spell chains keep flowing through a fight.
whyItMatters: FP hunger is what ends most caster fights, and this feeds the pool back with each kill instead of a flask. It suits sorcerers, incantation users, and any build that chains spells and skills in sequence.
whenToUse: Equip it once spellcasting is the main way a build wins fights. It is earned by trading the Remembrance of the Regal Ancestor, gained by defeating Regal Ancestor Spirit, to Finger Reader Enia, or by using one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate it.
name: Ancestral Spirit's Horn

desc: A talisman depicting three arrows. Carried by hunters of beasts. Increases the effective range of bows.
location: Loot: Stormgate (Limgrave) Found in a chest along the bridge over Stormgate's entrance. To access it, go to the southwest tower, kill the guards here, and then you can enter the area.
whatItIs: A talisman of three arrows worn by hunters of beasts. It stretches the effective range of bows, pushing the distance where a shot starts to fade further out.
whyItMatters: Ranged builds lose leverage when enemies close the gap, and this keeps arrows effective from further away so fights can be held at distance. A character who never carries a bow or crossbow gets nothing from the slot.
whenToUse: Equip it from the early game for any ranged build, since it is found early in Limgrave. It sits in a chest along the bridge over Stormgate's entrance, reached after killing the guards at the southwest tower.
name: Arrow's Reach Talisman

desc: A talisman composed of fletched and iron arrows. Increases the effective range of bows and raises attack power of arrows and bolts.
location: Loot: Fog Rift Fort (Scadu Altus) Found in a chest at the top of the southernmost rampart tower of the Fog Rift Fort. To access it, drop down a small ledge located to the left of the entrance of the building guarded by Black Knight Garrew, follow the wooden walkways around the cliff until it...
whatItIs: A two-in-one for bows: it stretches effective range and raises the attack power of arrows and bolts in the same slot. One talisman covers both the reach and the punch.
whyItMatters: It is the full-kit option for a ranged character, combining two effects a bow build usually chases separately. Where slots are tight, a single-effect talisman may fit better, but this does both jobs.
whenToUse: Equip it once a bow or crossbow build is underway. Requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion; it is looted from a chest at the top of the southernmost rampart tower of Fog Rift Fort, Scadu Altus, reached by dropping a small ledge to the left of the building guarded by Black Knight Garrew and following the wooden walkways around the cliff.
name: Arrow's Soaring Sting Talisman
effect: Increases the effective range of bows and raises attack power of arrows and bolts

desc: A talisman depicting three iron arrows. Carried by soldiers long ago. Raises attack power of arrows and bolts.
location: Loot: Impassable Greatbridge (Caelid) Obtained from a chest, atop the wooden siege tower, next to the Impassable Greatbridge Site of Grace.
whatItIs: Arrows and bolts carry more attack power while it is equipped, a pure damage bump for projectile weapons. It does nothing for melee, so the value lives entirely in bow and crossbow play.
whyItMatters: A ranged build's usual problem is punch, and this trades a slot for more damage per bolt without asking for any stat growth. A pure melee build gets nothing from it, so the slot is better spent elsewhere.
whenToUse: Equip it for a committed ranged build in the base game. It is obtained from a chest atop the wooden siege tower next to the Impassable Greatbridge Site of Grace, at the Impassable Greatbridge in Caelid.
name: Arrow's Sting Talisman
effect: Raises attack power of arrows and bolts

desc: An iron charm that resembles a mass of weapons. Boosts maximum equipment load. This talisman was derived from an unusual greatsword, once wielded by a hero hungry for vengeance.
location: Quest Item: Roundtable Hold Received from Nepheli Loux in Roundtable Hold, after talking to her at Stormveil Castle and defeating Godrick the Grafted.
whatItIs: An iron charm shaped like a mass of weapons. It raises maximum equipment load, letting a character field heavier armor and larger weapons than the stats alone allow.
whyItMatters: Heavy builds want thick armor without giving up mobility, and this is the unlock for that combination. Part of a family with stronger and weaker versions, so only one of them fits the slot at a time.
whenToUse: Equip it in the first hours for a heavy armor or greatsword build. It is received from Nepheli Loux in Roundtable Hold after talking to her at Stormveil Castle and defeating Godrick the Grafted.
name: Arsenal Charm

desc: An iron charm that resembles a mass of weaponry. Greatly boosts maximum equipment load. This talisman was derived from an unusual greatsword, once wielded by a hero hungry for vengeance.
location: Found in Altus Tunnel, looted from a corpse upon a wooden balcony overlooking a pit, where a monster fires rocks at you from above, with gravity magic. From the entrance to this area, drop to an overgrown root, and climb it to jump to an upper balcony, where the corpse lies.
whatItIs: An iron charm of piled weaponry that greatly raises maximum equipment load. It belongs to a family of talismans with stronger and weaker versions, and the variants cannot be equipped together.
whyItMatters: A dedicated heavy build wants the thickest armor with the quickest footwork, and a bigger load boost buys that combination. It is a solid choice for any armor-slugging character who wants more room in the load budget.
whenToUse: Swap it in once a heavy build is set and a bigger load boost is wanted. It is looted from a corpse on a wooden balcony in Altus Tunnel, reached by dropping to an overgrown root at the entrance, climbing it, and jumping to the upper balcony where the corpse lies.
name: Arsenal Charm +1

desc: An assassin's dagger, misshapen and stained in cerulean. Critical hits restore FP. This charm is modelled after the darkly gleaming blades used in the Night of Black Knives. Those which gave the demigods their first taste of death.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Black Knife Catacombs (Liurnia of the Lakes) Obtained from defeating the secret Black Knife Assassin hidden behind an Illusory Wall in the Black Knife Catacombs.
whatItIs: The cerulean-stained dagger pays out on every critical hit by restoring some FP. A caster can keep chaining spells off the crits it funds.
whyItMatters: Casters bleed FP on every spell, and this returns it right when the build lands its best hits. It is niche for pure melee characters who never cast, since the refund only fires on critical hits.
whenToUse: Equip it in a crit-heavy caster build, where backstabs and ripostes both feed the refund. It is a guaranteed drop from the secret Black Knife Assassin hidden behind an Illusory Wall in the Black Knife Catacombs, Liurnia of the Lakes.
name: Assassin's Cerulean Dagger

desc: An assassin's dagger, misshapen and stained in crimson. Critical hits restore HP. This charm is modelled after the darkly gleaming blades used in the night of Black Knives. Those which gave the demigods their first taste of death.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Deathtouched Catacombs (Limgrave) Obtained by defeating the Black Knife Assassin at the end of the catacombs.
whatItIs: Crimson-stained and misshapen, this dagger turns each critical hit into a small heal. The refund lands exactly when a backstab or riposte connects.
whyItMatters: A survivability tool for crit builds, since it replaces a flask sip with a well-timed backstab or riposte. It is niche for slow, trading-heavy builds that rarely land criticals.
whenToUse: Equip it any time a build leans on criticals, from backstabs to ripostes. It comes from the Black Knife Assassin at the end of the Deathtouched Catacombs, Limgrave.
name: Assassin's Crimson Dagger

desc: A talisman depicting an axe and a warrior. Enhances charge attacks. The Lord who led the Long March bore an axe, and his loyal warriors honored him by wielding axes of their own, making them very effective at dealing decisive blows.
location: Loot: Mistwood Ruins (Limgrave) Obtained from a chest in the cellar of Mistwood Ruins, eastern Limgrave. A Runebear lies very close to the entrance.
whatItIs: Held long, a weapon's charged swing hits harder while this is equipped. The boost only appears on charge attacks, so quick slashes are left alone.
whyItMatters: A greatsword with a charge attack is a reliable way to out-trade heavy armor, and this adds punch to exactly that committed move. For builds that never charge, the slot is better used elsewhere, making it niche outside that habit.
whenToUse: Equip it in a Strength or Faith build that favors weapons with charge attacks. It is obtained from a chest in the cellar of Mistwood Ruins in eastern Limgrave, with a Runebear lying very close to the entrance.
name: Axe Talisman

desc: A talisman depicting a wizened hand gently gripping a glintstone. Shortens casting speed for sorcery and incantations by the utmost, but increases damage taken. Count Ymir was known for his recitations. "One need only envision the romance of the stars above with adoration for stardust in one's heart to become a great sorcerer. Do so, and you will know love."
location: Received from: Count Ymir Ymir will reward the Tarnished with the Beloved Stardust and the Ruins Map (2nd) after using the Hole-Laden Necklace at the first Finger Ruins and returning to him.
whatItIs: Cast spells come out quicker while it is equipped, since it shortens casting speed for both sorcery and incantations. The price is that damage taken goes up for as long as it sits in the slot.
whyItMatters: A caster's spells take time to finish, and a faster cast lands before the enemy completes a combo. The raised damage taken makes it a risky trade, so it suits fights where the speed outweighs the exposure.
whenToUse: Equip it during tough boss fights once a spell build is fully geared. It requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, and it is received from Count Ymir after using the Hole-Laden Necklace at the first Finger Ruins and returning to him, who also hands over the Ruins Map (2nd).
name: Beloved Stardust
effect: Shortens casting speed for sorcery and incantations by the utmost, but increases damage taken

desc: A thin, blood-stained dagger. No longer fit for use. Raises attack power after each critical hit. Hornsent employed this to honorably end the suffering of a compatriot. After claiming numerous lives, the dagger is now broken, but has acquired a spectral aura.
location: Loot: Gravesite Plain Acquired from a chest at the top of Scorched Ruins.
whatItIs: Blood-stained and thin, the dagger raises attack power after each critical hit it lands. It rewards builds that lean on crits with extra punch at their best moments.
whyItMatters: Critical builds already chase backstabs and ripostes, and this turns every one of those into a damage bump. It is niche for builds that rarely crit, since the effect needs the crits to fire.
whenToUse: Equip it in a crit-focused build, since the effect pays off in every crit-heavy fight. The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion must be owned, and it is acquired from a chest at the top of Scorched Ruins, Gravesite Plain.
name: Blade of Mercy
effect: Raises attack power after each critical hit

desc: "Talisman depicting the blessed boon that is a droplet of the blue, luminescent sap of the Erdtree. Gradually restores FP." "It was once thought that the blessed sap of the Erdtree would drip from its boughs forever—but that age of plenty swiftly came to a close, and with time, the Erdtree became more an object of faith."
location: Loot: Church of Benediction (Gravesite Plain) Can be obtained at the Church of Benediction in front of the statue of Marika.
whatItIs: FP trickles back on its own while this sits in the slot, so a caster can keep spells moving between flasks. The effect is a slow, steady drip rather than a burst.
whyItMatters: FP is the fuel for every spell and skill, and a slow restore means fewer dry casts at the end of long fights. It is niche for pure melee builds, since they rarely spend the pool.
whenToUse: Equip it for a sustained spell build, since the slow refill keeps a caster going. It arrives with the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion and sits in front of the statue of Marika at the Church of Benediction in Gravesite Plain.
name: Blessed Blue Dew Talisman

desc: Talisman depicting a drop of the Erdtree's sap, a blessed boon. Gradually restores HP. It was once thought that the blessed sap of the Erdtree would drip from its boughs forever — but that age of plenty swiftly came to a close, and with time, the Erdtree became more an object of faith.
location: Loot: Leyndell, Royal Capital Obtained from a chest, west of the Divine Bridge Site of Grace. This area can be reached via an elevator, in the courtyard outside the Fortified Manor, or by using the sending gate in the Tower of Return, in the Weeping Peninsula.
whatItIs: HP trickles back on its own while it is equipped, a steady drip of healing through a whole fight. The effect is slow, so it rewards staying in the fight rather than escaping.
whyItMatters: It turns a fight that would end in a death into one that survives, because the heal accumulates while the character keeps pressing. Any build benefits from the free recovery.
whenToUse: Equip it once a build wants free recovery between fights. It waits in a chest west of the Divine Bridge Site of Grace in Leyndell, Royal Capital, reachable via the elevator in the courtyard outside the Fortified Manor or the sending gate in the Tower of Return in the Weeping Peninsula.
name: Blessed Dew Talisman

desc: A cloth doll depicting a dancer garbed in blue. An ancient heirloom of some sort. Raises attack power with lower equipment load. The dancer in blue represents a fairy, who in legend bestowed a flowing sword upon a blind swordsman. Blade in hand, the swordsman sealed away an ancient god - a god that was Rot itself.
location: Guranteed Drop: Highroad Cave (Limgrave) The Blue Dancer Charm is obtained by defeating the Guardian Golem in Highroad Cave.
whatItIs: Light feet pay off under this cloth doll: attack power rises while equipment load stays low. A heavy, fully-encased build gains nothing, so it favors nimble characters.
whyItMatters: It solves the classic tradeoff where thick armor kills attack power, letting a character stay agile without surrendering damage. A build running heavy armor will not see it, so it is niche outside the light-load route.
whenToUse: Equip it in the early game for a light, fast build. It is dropped by the Guardian Golem in Highroad Cave, Limgrave.
name: Blue Dancer Charm
effect: Raises attack power with lower equipment load

desc: A talisman adorned with blue feathers, once used in ancient death rituals. Raises defense when HP is low. The heart sings when one draws close to death, and thus does one cling so tenaciously to life - to render up a death worth offering.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Limgrave Obtained by defeating a Deathbird which appears east of Warmaster's Shack in Stormhill, near a ruin covered in Ruin Fragments and Sanctuary Stones at nighttime.
whatItIs: When the health bar runs low, defense comes up to meet it. The blue-feathered talisman turns a near-death moment into a window to keep swinging.
whyItMatters: It is a clutch tool for the moments a fight is going badly, softening exactly the hits that would finish the character off. Builds that never dip low get little from it, so it is niche without a reason to fight at low HP.
whenToUse: Equip it in the base game when a build wants a safety net at low HP. It is obtained by defeating a Deathbird that appears at nighttime east of Warmaster's Shack in Stormhill, near a ruin covered in Ruin Fragments and Sanctuary Stones.
name: Blue-Feathered Branchsword
effect: Raises defense when HP is low

desc: Talisman depicting a yellow ancient dragon. Boosts lightning damage negation. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Loot: Stormveil Castle Obtained from a corpse just before the bridge leading eastward, to the Divine Tower of Limgrave.
whatItIs: The face of this one shows a yellow ancient dragon, but the real work happens in the resistances. Lightning damage negation is boosted while it is equipped.
whyItMatters: Lightning attacks carve through even well-armored builds, and this softens them. It belongs to a line of similar talismans, some stronger and some weaker, and a character wears just one at a time.
whenToUse: Equip it in the base game once lightning damage starts hurting. It is looted from a corpse just before the bridge leading eastward to the Divine Tower of Limgrave, in Stormveil Castle.
name: Boltdrake Talisman

desc: Talisman depicting a duo of yellow ancient dragons. Greatly boosts lightning damage negation. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Loot: Altus Plateau Acquired from a corpse within a wooden shed guarded by stray dogs in Old Altus Tunnel.
whatItIs: Same dragon motif, a bigger effect: lightning damage negation is greatly boosted while it is equipped. One of a family of similar talismans, with stronger and weaker versions, and a build equips just one of them.
whyItMatters: A build that keeps getting clipped by lightning attacks gains more breathing room under the bigger boost. The family shares one talisman slot, so pick one variant and leave the rest.
whenToUse: Swap it in when lightning pressure is the main threat and a bigger negation bump is wanted. It is acquired from a corpse within a wooden shed guarded by stray dogs in Old Altus Tunnel, Altus Plateau.
name: Boltdrake Talisman +1

desc: Talisman depicting a trio of yellow ancient dragons. Vastly boosts lightning damage negation. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Loot: Crumbling Farum Azula Obtained from a corpse near the Dragon Temple Rooftop Site of Grace. From the Rooftop Grace proceed southeast to the arena of an Ancient Dragon. Proceed east to the edge of the arena, where you can drop to a series of platforms, leading to an isolated building....
whatItIs: Three yellow ancient dragons mark this one, and the effect matches the family's purpose. Lightning damage negation is vastly boosted while it is equipped.
whyItMatters: Fights loaded with lightning become calmer under a bigger negation bump, which is exactly what a build lacking raw lightning resistances needs. Outside those situations the slot is better spent elsewhere, so it stays niche.
whenToUse: Equip it in the base game when lightning-heavy enemies are the main problem. It is obtained from a corpse near the Dragon Temple Rooftop Site of Grace in Crumbling Farum Azula, reached by proceeding southeast from the Rooftop Grace to the arena of an Ancient Dragon, then east to the edge and dropping to a series of platforms toward an isolated building.
name: Boltdrake Talisman +2

desc: Talisman with a large depiction of a yellow ancient dragon. Boosts lightning damage negation by the utmost. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: It can be found at Shadow Keep. From the Storehouse: First Floor site of grace, take the stairs up to the second floor and find a dead-end with several shade protectors. Jump over the railing to reach a room with the talisman, then use the lever to move the bookcase and re-emerge near the site...
whatItIs: Once slotted, it absorbs a share of the lightning damage that would otherwise land on the character, so charged hits sting far less. There is nothing to activate, and the effect simply runs for as long as it is equipped.
whyItMatters: Lightning is a damage type few starting builds plan for, and this solves the problem of getting melted by charged strikes without spending any stats on resistance. It is part of a family with stronger and weaker versions.
whenToUse: Equip it when lightning attacks suddenly start landing hard, then swap it out once the threat is over. It needs the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion before it can be found, and it waits in Shadow Keep, up the stairs from the Storehouse: First Floor site of grace, past the shade protectors, and over the railing into the room that holds the talisman.
name: Boltdrake Talisman +3

desc: A talisman depicting the horns of a bull-goat. Raises poise. Bull-goats are associated with the stout and mighty Tragoth, said to be unflinching in combat - now a silent comrade to those who fight.
location: Obtained from a corpse, in Dragonbarrow Cave, in northern Greyoll's Dragonbarrow, below the Minor Erdtree. Head left after entering the Runebear's room to find it.
whatItIs: Wearing it raises poise, so enemy hits are less likely to interrupt a weapon swing or a spell in progress. The effect stays on for the whole time it is equipped.
whyItMatters: Getting poise-broken mid-attack is a frustrating moment in any fight, because the character reels and opens a follow-up window. It suits heavy, slow weapon builds and anyone whose swings keep getting interrupted.
whenToUse: Equip it against enemies whose hits interrupt attacks, and drop it in fights that rely on dodging instead. It lies on a corpse in Dragonbarrow Cave in northern Greyoll's Dragonbarrow below the Minor Erdtree, to the left after entering the Runebear's room.
name: Bull-Goat's Talisman

desc: A talisman adorned with the royal crest. Lowers FP consumed by skills. n honor said to have once been awarded to Carian knights who served as direct retainers to the kingdom's princesses. Now there is only one princess: Ranni, daughter of Rennala.
location: Purchase: Smithing Master Iji (Liurnia of the Lakes) Becomes available for 5000 after meeting either of the following two criterias: Exhausting Blaidd the Half-Wolf's dialogue at the Weeping Evergaol after defeating Bloodhound Knight Darriwil, then selecting the "Blaidd sent me" dialogue option...
whatItIs: While equipped, it lowers the FP cost of weapon skills and incantations, so each cast drains a smaller slice of the pool. It does not add FP, it only makes every use cheaper.
whyItMatters: A caster running out of FP mid-boss is stuck with a sword, and this stretches each pool further. It is a sharp tool for spell and skill heavy builds, and it pairs well with anything that restores FP.
whenToUse: Equip it for spell builds and skill heavy setups, and skip it on a pure melee character. It is sold by Smithing Master Iji in Liurnia of the Lakes, and it unlocks after defeating Bloodhound Knight Darriwil and exhausting Blaidd the Half-Wolf's dialogue at Weeping Evergaol.
name: Carian Filigreed Crest

desc: A medallion with cerulean amber inlaid. Boosts maximum FP. The Erdtree's old sap becomes amber, treasured as the most precious of jewels in the age of Godfrey, the first Elden Lord. A primordial life energy resides inside.
location: Drop: Lakeside Crystal Cave (Liurnia of the Lakes) Obtained by defeating the Bloodhound Knight in Lakeside Crystal Cave.
whatItIs: A medallion that raises maximum FP for as long as it sits in a talisman slot. More FP means more room for incantations and weapon skills between refills.
whyItMatters: FP runs dry fast in a long boss fight, and a bigger pool delays the moment spells stop. The medallion belongs to a family with stronger and weaker versions, so treat it as the entry point for any starved caster.
whenToUse: Equip it early on a caster or a skill heavy build, and keep it until a stronger version of it turns up. It drops from the Bloodhound Knight in Lakeside Crystal Cave in Liurnia of the Lakes.
name: Cerulean Amber Medallion

desc: A medallion with cerulean amber inlaid. Greatly boosts maximum FP. The Erdtree's old sap becomes amber, treasured as the most precious of jewels in the age of Godfrey, the first Elden Lord. A primordial life energy resides inside.
location: Loot: Castle Sol (Mountaintops of the Giants) Obtained from a corpse hanging from a wooden platform attached to the southern wall of Castle Sol. From Church of the Eclipse, head left to the front of the church, left through a door, right, up a ladder, southwest to a tower, which can be circled...
whatItIs: An upgraded Cerulean Amber Medallion that raises maximum FP by a wider margin. The effect is the same, only the pool is deeper.
whyItMatters: For a caster, the difference shows up as one more incantation before the pool runs dry. The design comes in stronger and weaker variants, and it helps most in long attrition fights.
whenToUse: Equip it whenever the base medallion is too thin and the next step up is out of reach. It is looted from a corpse hanging from a wooden platform on the southern wall of Castle Sol in the Mountaintops of the Giants, approached from the Church of the Eclipse.
name: Cerulean Amber Medallion +1

desc: A medallion with cerulean amber inlaid. Vastly boosts maximum FP. The Erdtree's old sap becomes amber, treasured as the most precious of jewels in the age of Godfrey, the first Elden Lord. A primordial life energy resides inside.
location: Loot: Lunar Estate Ruins (Liurnia of the Lakes) Obtained from a chest, in the cellar of Lunar Estate Ruins, in southern Liurnia of the Lakes. This area of Liurnia can only be accessed from underground, after progressing through Grand Cloister. The cellar is hidden beneath an illusory floor, and...
whatItIs: One step up the line, the medallion boosts maximum FP further. It works exactly like its siblings, with a wider pool.
whyItMatters: Incantations and weapon skills chain together, and the bigger pool lets a caster hold a full combo instead of pausing for a flask mid-chain. Weaker and stronger members of the family are out there to swap into.
whenToUse: Equip it on spell builds once the earlier medallions no longer carry the load. It waits in a chest in the cellar of Lunar Estate Ruins in southern Liurnia of the Lakes, hidden under an illusory floor, and the pocket is only reachable underground after progressing through Grand Cloister.
name: Cerulean Amber Medallion +2

desc: "A medallion with cerulean amber inlaid. Boosts maximum FP by the utmost." The Erdtree's old sap becomes amber, treasured as the most precious of jewels in the age of Godfrey, the first Elden Lord. A primordial life energy resides inside.
location: Drop: Scorpion River Catacombs (Rauh Base) Obtained as a reward after defeating the Death Knight in Scorpion River Catacombs.
whatItIs: The DLC cut of the medallion boosts maximum FP by a wide margin. Slotted, the pool is simply bigger for as long as it stays equipped.
whyItMatters: Sustained spell combat dries out smaller pools, and the deeper one here keeps the casting going. The game has other, stronger and weaker versions of it.
whenToUse: Equip it for long spell fights where FP goes first. The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is required to find it, and it drops from the Death Knight in Scorpion River Catacombs in Rauh Base.
name: Cerulean Amber Medallion +3
effect: Boosts maximum FP by the utmost

desc: A cerulean-colored talisman patterned after an Erdtree seed. Boosts FP restoration from the Flask of Cerulean Tears. The Erdtree was once perfect and eternal, and thus was it believed that Erdtree seeds could not exist.
location: Loot: Carian Study Hall (Liurnia of the Lakes) Obtained from a corpse in un-flipped version of the Carian Study Hall, located in the eastern region of Liurnia of the Lakes. The corpse can be found on the upper-most level of rafters in the tower, which you can climb to with ladders.
whatItIs: Equipped, it boosts the FP restoration from the Flask of Cerulean Tears, so each sip refills a larger share of the pool. The flask itself is unchanged; only the refill is deeper.
whyItMatters: A caster can pour a full flask back in seconds and still finish the fight dry, and this closes that gap. Stronger and weaker versions of the same design exist, and it suits builds that lean on continuous casting.
whenToUse: Equip it on spell builds that drink the flask between boss phases. It lies on a corpse in the un-flipped version of Carian Study Hall in Liurnia of the Lakes, up on the topmost level of the tower's rafters reached by ladders.
name: Cerulean Seed Talisman
effect: Boosts FP restoration from Flask of Cerulean Tears

desc: A cerulean-colored talisman pattered after an Erdtree seed. Greatly boosts FP restoration from the Flask of Cerulean Tears. The Erdtree seed of this talisman was presumed to be an object of myth. This age-old artifact also depicts the Two Fingers, perhaps harkening back to the birth of the Erdtree.
location: Quest Reward: Finger Ruins of Dheo (Scaduview) The Cerulean Seed Talisman +1 is received after using the Hole-Laden Necklace to ring the bell at the center of a large ring of stone fingers at the Finger Ruins of Dheo. The ring of fingers is shown on the Ruins Map (2nd) acquired from Count Ymir...
whatItIs: An upgraded Cerulean Seed Talisman that makes each Flask of Cerulean Tears refill deeper. The drinking ritual is unchanged; the restoration is simply bigger.
whyItMatters: For an incantation build, the difference is one extra spell before the flask empties. More and less potent siblings of the design are out there.
whenToUse: Equip it on heavy casting builds, especially against enemies that punish long downtime. It is behind the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, and it is earned in Finger Ruins of Dheo in Scaduview by using the Hole-Laden Necklace to ring the bell at the center of the ring of stone fingers, a spot marked on the Ruins Map (2nd) acquired from Count Ymir.
name: Cerulean Seed Talisman +1
effect: Boosts FP restoration from the Flask of Cerulean Tears

desc: An accoutrement worn by the ancestral followers. Raises focus. (Focus governs resistance to sleep and madness.) Said to be a budding horn. The ancestral followers believed that the horns of a long-lived beast continue to bud like antlers, over and over again, until the beast one day becomes an ancestral spirit.
location: Obtained from a corpse, lying on the stairs in northern Siofra River, near the Below the Well Sites of Grace (this is the entrance area to the region if using the Deep Siofra Well in Caelid).
whatItIs: Worn, it raises focus, the hidden stat that governs resistance to sleep and madness. Buildups of those effects then creep in more slowly while it is equipped.
whyItMatters: Sleep and madness buildup can end a fight from the inside, and a higher focus value delays that moment. Siblings of this design run both stronger and weaker.
whenToUse: Equip it before entering sleep and madness heavy zones, and drop it once the threat is gone. It lies on a corpse on the stairs in northern Siofra River near the Below the Well Sites of Grace, the entrance area when using Deep Siofra Well in Caelid.
name: Clarifying Horn Charm

desc: An accoutrement worn by the ancestral followers. Greatly raises focus. (Focus governs resistance to sleep and madness.) Said to be a budding horn. The ancestral followers believed that the horns of a long-lived beast continue to bud like antlers, over and over again, until the beast one day becomes an ancestral spirit.
location: Obtained from a corpse, in Siofra River, accessed from Nokron, Eternal City. From Mimic Tear, head northeast along the aqueduct, to the spot where it collapses to the left, onto the field below. Head down here, and northeast again, to drop down to the lower level of the aqueduct. Continue to the...
whatItIs: The step up in the Clarifying Horn Charm line raises focus by a wider margin. Sleep and madness buildup then crawl in at a slower pace.
whyItMatters: Fights that lean on sleep effects reward patience, and the bigger focus pool buys more of it. Other, less and more potent forms of this design exist.
whenToUse: Equip it in the same sleep and madness heavy spots, whenever the base version runs out of headroom. It waits on a corpse in Siofra River, reached from Nokron, Eternal City, after heading northeast from Mimic Tear along the aqueduct and dropping down where it collapses.
name: Clarifying Horn Charm +1

desc: Ceremonial accoutrement worn by hornsent. Vastly raises focus. (Focus governs resistance to sleep and madness.) Horns are sublime artifacts to hornsent, and their presence confirms the belief that they are a chosen people. Only the repeated sprouting of fresh horns can create a tangled horn, which is viewed as an irrefutable symbol of primacy.
location: Clarifying Horn Charm +2 is found in the Lamenter's Gaol. Drop down into a rat-infested area and take the straight path forward. The talisman is located in the next area on a corpse along the right side.
whatItIs: Beyond the base design, the focus rise here is wider. Sleep and madness pressure eases further while it is equipped.
whyItMatters: Long fights in madness-prone areas stop being a slow leak, and a build can spend its attention on offense. The family stretches in both directions as well.
whenToUse: Equip it in sleep and madness heavy zones where the earlier versions stop being enough. It requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion to exist, and it is found in Lamenter's Gaol, on a corpse along the right side of the area just past the rat-infested drop.
name: Clarifying Horn Charm +2

desc: A talisman depicting a claw and an assassin. Enhances jump attacks. The assassins of Ravenmount are killers by trade. They assail their victims while dressed as birds of prey.
location: Guaranteed Loot: Stormveil Castle Obtained from a corpse in Stormveil Castle, on top of a watchtower. From Rampart Tower Site of Grace, head through the southern door, hang a right, and climb the spiral staircase. Enter the outer hallway, and circle around to the exit that leads to a rooftop....
whatItIs: Equipped, it enhances jump attacks, so landing from a leap hits harder than an ordinary attack. No stat requirement and no activation.
whyItMatters: Jump attacks are a reliable way to punish a charging boss, and a boosted version of the move turns a nudge into a real damage window. It is niche for purely horizontal brawlers, and sharp for any build that plays from height.
whenToUse: Equip it against large enemies that charge across open ground, and skip it on builds that never jump-attack. It is guaranteed loot from a corpse atop a watchtower in Stormveil Castle, reached from the Rampart Tower Site of Grace by climbing the spiral staircase and circling the outer hallway out to the rooftop.
name: Claw Talisman

desc: A talisman given by the jars to their friends. Raises potency of thrown jars. Though the jars are brought to life by human flesh and blood, they are all rather kindly folk. Perhaps they were made to be better than their innards.
location: Quest: Jar-Bairn Obtained from Jar-Bairn in Jarburg, after completing his questline, by giving him Alexander's Innards. Exhaust his dialogue and reset the game, the talisman will be here he was once seated.
whatItIs: It raises the potency of thrown pots, making each jar lob do more damage. Only the jar and pot throwing moves benefit, not other weapons.
whyItMatters: Thrown pots are a free ranged nudge that asks nothing of a build, and a boosted version of them adds a real damage option in close. It is niche outside pot-heavy setups.
whenToUse: Equip it when a build wants a cheap ranged nudge between close-range swaps. It comes from Jar-Bairn in Jarburg after giving him Alexander's Innards and completing his questline, and the talisman sits where he was once seated.
name: Companion Jar

desc: Talisman put together from dark cloth, with a lustrous sheen. Completely conceals the wearer's presence while crouching at a distance from foes. Part of one of the concealing veils used by the assassins on the Night of Black Knives.
location: Obtained by defeating the Black Knife Assassin in Sage's Cave in western Altus Plateau.
whatItIs: While equipped, the character is completely concealed while crouching at a distance from foes. Stand up, close the gap, or stop crouching, and the hiding is off.
whyItMatters: It creates a real window to slip past patrols or to reset a chase without a fight. It is niche outside crouch-and-sneak moments, but in those moments it is the whole strategy.
whenToUse: Equip it for sections filled with hostile patrols: crouch at range, then walk through as if unseen. It drops from the Black Knife Assassin in Sage's Cave in western Altus Plateau.
name: Concealing Veil
effect: Conceals wearer while crouching away from foes

desc: Small mysterious bottle with a dark mist sealed within. Eliminates all sound made by the wearer during movement. A ritual implement used by Roundtable Hold assassins. There was a time when Tarnished who had strayed from guidance feared nothing more than utter silence.
location: Obtained by killing Rileigh the Idle, in Altus Plateau, after invading their world to complete the second Volcano Manor assassination.
whatItIs: Equipped, it silences all the sound the wearer makes while moving, so footsteps stop giving away position. Combat noise is not included; only movement sound goes quiet.
whyItMatters: It solves the problem of being detected from a distance while sneaking, which no other stat can fix. It is niche outside stealth runs, but it makes those runs actually possible.
whenToUse: Equip it while crouching through patrolled areas or dropping from a height. It is obtained by killing Rileigh the Idle in Altus Plateau, after invading their world to complete the second Volcano Manor assassination.
name: Crepus's Vial
effect: Eliminates all sound made by the wearer during movement

desc: A medallion with Crimson amber inlaid. Boosts maximum HP. The Erdtree's old sap becomes amber, treasured as the most precious of jewels in the age of Godfrey, the first Elden Lord. A primordial life energy resides inside.
location: Keepsake: May be chosen as a Keepsake when creating a new character. Purchase: Weeping Peninsula (Limgrave) Purchased for 1,500 Runes from the Nomadic Merchant at the Castle Morne Rampart Site of Grace.
whatItIs: A medallion that raises maximum HP for the whole time it is slotted. Nothing to activate, nothing to manage.
whyItMatters: More HP turns a one-shot into a survivable hit and buys time to learn a boss. The family it belongs to has stronger and weaker members.
whenToUse: Take it as a Keepsake at character creation, or buy it from the Nomadic Merchant at the Castle Morne Rampart Site of Grace on the Weeping Peninsula in Limgrave. Leave it equipped until a stronger version turns up.
name: Crimson Amber Medallion

desc: A medallion with Crimson amber inlaid. Greatly boosts maximum HP. The Erdtree's old sap becomes amber, treasured as the most precious of jewels in the age of Godfrey, the first Elden Lord. A primordial life energy resides inside.
location: Loot: Volcano Manor (Mt. Gelmir) Obtained from a corpse in Volcano Manor. From Prison Town Church, head out the eastern door, and right. Proceed along the main path through the town, past an Iron Virgin until reaching a brick courtyard, in front of a building whose door is locked by a...
whatItIs: An upgraded Crimson Amber Medallion that deepens the maximum HP pool. The effect is the same, only the buffer is thicker.
whyItMatters: One extra breath of HP is the difference between dying on a late boss hit and having room for one more heal. Siblings of the medallion run both directions in power.
whenToUse: Equip it on any build the moment the base medallion stops covering the damage spike. It is looted from a corpse in Volcano Manor in Mt. Gelmir, found from Prison Town Church by heading out the eastern door, turning right, and following the main path past the Iron Virgin into the brick courtyard.
name: Crimson Amber Medallion +1

desc: A medallion with Crimson amber inlaid. Vastly boosts maximum HP. The Erdtree's old sap becomes amber, treasured as the most precious of jewels in the age of Godfrey, the first Elden Lord. A primordial life energy resides inside.
location: Loot: Subterranean Shunning-Grounds (Leyndell, Ashen Capital) Pillaged from corpse which can found on a wooden beam that can only be reached after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade. Once the ashen version of Leyndell is available, head south from the "Leyndell, Capital of Ash" site of grace...
whatItIs: One more step in the family, the HP pool deepens further. Slotted, the character simply survives hits that would have been lethal.
whyItMatters: Late bosses deal damage that smaller pools cannot weather, and the extra headroom changes how aggressively a build can trade blows. Weaker and stronger forms of the medallion are scattered around.
whenToUse: Equip it in the endgame stretch after the ashen capital opens up. It is looted from a corpse on a wooden beam in Subterranean Shunning-Grounds in Leyndell, Ashen Capital, reachable only after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade, off the Leyndell, Capital of Ash site of grace.
name: Crimson Amber Medallion +2

desc: A medallion with crimson amber inlaid. Boosts maximum HP by the utmost. The Erdtree's old sap becomes amber, treasured as the most precious of jewels in the age of Godfrey, the first Elden Lord. These medallions, of the largest variety, were conferred to Godwyn's inner circle of distinguished golden knights.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Fog Rift Catacombs (Gravesite Plain) Acquired by defeating the Death Knight encountered at the end of the Fog Rift Catacombs.
whatItIs: A Crimson Amber Medallion variant that boosts maximum HP by a wide margin. Everything else about how it works matches the base-game versions.
whyItMatters: A deeper HP pool shrinks the window a boss needs to punish a slow reaction. Both stronger and weaker members of the family exist.
whenToUse: Equip it whenever the earlier medallions no longer cover the incoming damage. The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion gates this one, and it is a guaranteed drop from the Death Knight at the end of Fog Rift Catacombs in Gravesite Plain.
name: Crimson Amber Medallion +3

desc: A crimson-colored talisman patterned after an Erdtree seed. Boosts HP restoration from the Flask of Crimson Tears. The Erdtree was once perfect and eternal, and thus was it believed that Erdtree seeds could not exist.
location: Loot: Sainted Hero's Grave (Altus Plateau) Obtained from a corpse that behind a semi-transparent fog wall, near the beginning of the dungeon, which can be unlocked by inserting one Stonesword Key into the adjacent imp statue.
whatItIs: A seed-styled talisman that makes each Flask of Crimson Tears restore more HP while it sits in the talisman slot. It has no activation step and no upkeep.
whyItMatters: Flask healing shows up in nearly every fight, so a stronger flask covers a mistimed dodge or a heavy boss hit without spending any stat points. It is part of a family with stronger and weaker versions, and this base form is a light, easy first pick.
whenToUse: Equip it on Altus Plateau once the Sainted Hero's Grave is open. The corpse sits behind a semi-transparent fog wall near the start of the dungeon, unlocked by inserting one Stonesword Key into the adjacent imp statue. Keep it on through early fights and swap it out when a different talisman better fits the build.
name: Crimson Seed Talisman
effect: Boosts HP regeneration from Flask of Crimson Tears

desc: A crimson-colored talisman pattered after an Erdtree seed. Greatly boosts HP restoration from the Flask of Crimson Tears. The Erdtree seed of this talisman was presumed to be an object of myth. This age-old artifact also depicts the Two Fingers, perhaps harkening back to the birth of the Erdtree.
location: Quest Reward: Finger Ruins of Rhia (Cerulean Coast) The Crimson Seed Talisman +1 is received after using the Hole-Laden Necklace to ring the bell at the center of a large ring of stone fingers at the Finger Ruins of Rhia. The ring of fingers is shown on the Ruins Map acquired from Count Ymir...
whatItIs: The upgraded Crimson Seed token, and it boosts HP recovery from the Flask of Crimson Tears. Nothing to press or manage once it is slotted.
whyItMatters: A flask that returns more HP turns a boss hit that would have been fatal into a recoverable one, and that margin matters most in long, drawn-out fights. It is part of a family that has both stronger and weaker versions, so expect to see similar tokens elsewhere too.
whenToUse: Reaching the ring where this drops depends on the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. In the Finger Ruins of Rhia on the Cerulean Coast, ring the bell at the center of the large stone-finger ring using the Hole-Laden Necklace to receive it, and the Ruins Map from Count Ymir marks where the ring sits.
name: Crimson Seed Talisman +1
effect: Boosts HP regeneration from Flask of Crimson Tears

desc: A talisman fashioned from feathers that embody the aspects of various creatures. Said to have grown on the human body long ago. Improves the effectiveness of dodge rolls, but increases damage taken at all times. A vestige of the crucible of primordial life. Born partially of devolution, it was considered a signifier of the divine in ancient times, but is now increasingly disdained as an impurity as civilization has advanced.
location: Obtained from a corpse in Auriza Hero's Grave in the Leyndell, Royal Capital region. Make your way to the area where two chariots ride side-by-side, up and down a slope. At the bottom of this slope is a corpse, hanging off of a ledge above a pit. Drop into the pit from where this corpse lies to...
whatItIs: Feathers woven into a talisman that makes dodge rolls more effective while raising the damage taken at all times. It is always active while equipped, with no toggle.
whyItMatters: A more effective roll is the difference between escaping a heavy slam and eating it, which suits aggressive, roll-heavy play around big enemies. The constant extra damage taken is the trade, so it is a niche pick for anyone who already dodges cleanly.
whenToUse: Pick it up in Auriza Hero's Grave in the Leyndell, Royal Capital region. The corpse hangs off a ledge above a pit where two chariots ride up and down a slope, so drop into the pit from the ledge to grab it. Equip it for fights where constant rolling is the plan, and remove it before any fight that relies on staying up close.
name: Crucible Feather Talisman
effect: Improves dodge rolling but increases damage taken

desc: A talisman fashioned from a bony knot that embodies the aspects of various creatures. Said to have grown on the human body long ago. Reduces damage and impact of headshots taken. A vestige of the crucible of primordial life. Born partially of devolution, it was considered a signifier of the divine in ancient times, but is now increasingly disdained as an impurity as civilization has advanced.
location: Obtained by killing the Omenkiller boss in Village of the Albinaurics, in southern Liurnia of the Lakes.
whatItIs: A bony knot worn as a talisman that reduces both the damage and the impact of headshots taken. The effect is passive and constant while it is equipped.
whyItMatters: Head hits knock a character around harder, so softening them keeps a build on its feet through enemy sweeps and lunges that would otherwise end the fight. It is a steady shield against the hit type that most often sends a character flying.
whenToUse: Drop by the Omenkiller boss in Village of the Albinaurics in southern Liurnia of the Lakes to claim it. Equip it during boss fights where head strikes are frequent, and it suits lighter builds that cannot survive a clean head hit.
name: Crucible Knot Talisman
effect: Reduces damage and impact of headshots

desc: A talisman fashioned from a scale that embodies the aspects of various creatures. Said to have grown on the human body long ago. Reduces damage taken from critical hits. A vestige of the crucible of primordial life. Born partially of devolution, it was considered a signifier of the divine in ancient times, but is now increasingly disdained as an impurity as civilization has advanced.
location: Obtained from a corpse in Leyndell Catacombs, in the Leyndell, Royal Capital region. The corpse is guarded by an Omen, which can be reached by lowering a fire-breathing pillar, and riding it back upward to reach the upper-level of the room.
whatItIs: A scale talisman that reduces the damage taken from critical hits, so a critical strike lands for less. It works passively for as long as it stays slotted.
whyItMatters: Critical hits arrive with the enemy's best-timed swings, and each one removes a large chunk of HP. Softening that hit type extends a fight and keeps a build standing when perfect enemy timing would otherwise finish it.
whenToUse: Find it on a corpse in Leyndell Catacombs in the Leyndell, Royal Capital region. The guard is an Omen, and the way in is to lower a fire-breathing pillar, ride it back up, and step onto the upper level of the room. Slot it before boss fights where the enemy punishes openings with critical strikes.
name: Crucible Scale Talisman
effect: Reduces damage taken from critical hits

desc: A talisman depicting a raised spear on a backdrop of flames, in remembrance of the lives lost in the sacred crusade led by Messmer. Raises attack power after defeating an enemy. The warriors who fought in the crusade set aside both honor and mercy to wantonly impale and scorch those deemed impure. Those who felt invigorated by each cry of death were the same men who were certain of the sanctity of the campaign.
location: Guaranteed Drop from vanquishing the invading Fire Knight Queelign for the first time at either of the following locations: Belurat, Tower Settlement - Invades in the spiraltree courtyard northeast of the Small Private Altar site of grace. Church of the Crusade - Invades at the northwestern side...
whatItIs: The raised-spear icon backed by flames raises attack power after defeating an enemy while it sits in the slot. It is passive and needs no input.
whyItMatters: Sweeps through groups of enemies hit harder as defeats accumulate, which suits a build that fights in packs and chases down stragglers. It fits pack-based clears better than slow one-at-a-time boss work, since few defeats bring little boost.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion has to be active for this invader to appear. It is a guaranteed drop from defeating the invading Fire Knight Queelign for the first time. That invader appears at either Belurat, Tower Settlement near the Small Private Altar site of grace or at the Church of the Crusade.
name: Crusade Insignia
effect: Raises attack power after defeating an enemy

desc: A talisman depicting a curved sword and a swordsman. Enhances guard counters. It is said that a blind swordsman was the originator of this technique -- the art of allowing one's opponent to strike so as to leave them vulnerable to a well-timed reply.
location: Loot: Stormveil Castle (Limgrave) Obtained from a chest in Stormveil Castle, in the room where the player character gets locked-in with the Banished Knight. This area is only accessible by using the secret side-entrance, suggested by Gatekeeper Gostoc.
whatItIs: Swordsman and curved blade on this token, which enhances guard counters for as long as it is slotted. The boost applies to every guard counter landed.
whyItMatters: A well-timed guard counter already turns the enemy's own attack back on them, and making that reply hit harder rewards a patient, parry-minded style. It suits builds that lean on the shield and the counter window instead of rolling away.
whenToUse: It waits in a chest inside Stormveil Castle in Limgrave, in the room where the Banished Knight locks the door. The route in is the secret side entrance that Gatekeeper Gostoc points out, so visit him first and then come back for the chest.
name: Curved Sword Talisman

desc: Disturbing likeness of a woman whose skin was flayed. She smiles with a serene tenderness. Increases damage taken. It is said that this woman, named Daedicar, indulged in every form of adultery and wicked pleasure imaginable, giving birth to a myriad of grotesque children.
location: Quest Item: Volcano Manor Obtained from Rya towards the end of her questline, after she realizes the truth of her origin and requests the player to kill her. She will drop it if she is killed. It can also be found lying on the floor after Rya leaves the room: Either after giving her the Tonic of...
whatItIs: An unsettling likeness of a serene, flayed woman that does the opposite of most talismans: it increases damage taken. It is active for as long as it sits in the slot.
whyItMatters: There is no combat benefit to wearing it, and it is a niche item of interest mostly for the quest that hands it over. A character who equips it falls faster in every fight, and no build gains an edge from that.
whenToUse: It comes from Volcano Manor towards the end of Rya's questline. After she realizes the truth of her origin and asks to be killed, defeating her drops it, and it can also be found lying on the floor after she leaves the room. There is no fight where equipping it helps, so keep it stored.
name: Daedicar's Woe

desc: A talisman depicting a dagger and a surgeon. Enhances critical hits. The white-garbed field surgeons come to the aid of friend and foe alike by dealing a final deadly thrust to spare them from the prolonged agony of a mortal wound. A sense of mercy is a catalyst for bloodlust.
location: Loot: Volcano Manor (Mt. Gelmir) Obtained from a corpse in Volcano Manor. From the throne room, just before the waygate leading to Audience Pathway, head west up the stairs, and unlock the semi-transparent fog wall there, by inserting 2 Stonesword Keys into the adjacent imp statue. Upon reaching...
whatItIs: Dagger and white-garbed surgeon on this token, and it enhances critical hits while slotted. No activation is required.
whyItMatters: Critical strikes land harder, and making them hit harder still rewards any style built around backstabs, ripostes, and opening a foe's guard. It is felt strongly on builds that already win those moments and want more from each one.
whenToUse: Loot it from a corpse in Volcano Manor on Mt. Gelmir. From the throne room, head west up the stairs just before the waygate to Audience Pathway, then unlock the semi-transparent fog wall by inserting 2 Stonesword Keys into the adjacent imp statue, and slot it in before fights won by opening combos and critical strikes.
name: Dagger Talisman

desc: Wrought iron talisman depicting a massive ancient dragon. Enormously boosts physical damage negation. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Loot: Drainage Channel (Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree) Obtained from inside a chest. From the Drainage Channel Site of Grace, head east and travel along tree roots, branches, and buttresses to reach the roof of the nearby church, which is full of Pests. Drop through a hole in the roof, and...
whatItIs: Wrought-iron work depicting a massive ancient dragon, and it enormously boosts physical damage negation while equipped. Nothing to manage.
whyItMatters: Physical damage is everywhere in the early hours, so negating more of it keeps a build standing through the heaviest swings. It is a straightforward damage sponge, and the problem it solves is simply dying to big melee hits.
whenToUse: It is a chest loot find in Drainage Channel at Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree. From the Drainage Channel site of grace, head east along the tree roots and branches until reaching the roof of the nearby church where Pests roam, then drop through a hole in the roof. Equip it during fights against big, slow physical hitters.
name: Dragoncrest Greatshield Talisman

desc: Wrought iron talisman depicting an ancient dragon. Boosts physical damage negation. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Obtained from a corpse that lies on the ground, near Bestial Sanctum, in northern Greyoll's Dragonbarrow. From the front door of the sanctum, head southwest around the side of the sanctum, until reaching a cliff that overlooks a large tree root, close enough to drop to.
whatItIs: Iron and an ancient dragon's shape, and this token boosts physical damage negation for the duration it is slotted. It works passively on every physical hit it sees.
whyItMatters: A flat reduction in physical damage makes every enemy swing hurt less, which is exactly the cushion a fragile build needs while learning a boss's rhythm. Stronger and weaker versions of this effect exist in its family.
whenToUse: It lies on a corpse near Bestial Sanctum in northern Greyoll's Dragonbarrow. From the front door of the sanctum, walk southwest around the side until reaching a cliff that overlooks a large tree root close enough to drop to. Equip it whenever a physical-heavy fight is ahead and HP is tight.
name: Dragoncrest Shield Talisman

desc: :Wrought iron talisman depicting a duo of ancient dragons. Greatly boosts physical damage negation. :The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Obtained from the Sainted Hero's Grave in central Altus Plateau. In the room with the giant falling blade traps, jump on top of the first one to ride it upwards, and jump to the ledge on the left. Follow this path to reach a room that has a pair of semi-transparent fog walls, locked by an imp...
whatItIs: Twin dragons carved in wrought iron, and this token greatly boosts physical damage negation while it sits in the slot. The effect is constant and needs no input.
whyItMatters: More negation means the same enemy swing that hurt a lot now shaves HP instead, stretching every exchange in a boss fight. It belongs to the same family of tokens with stronger and weaker versions.
whenToUse: It is inside the Sainted Hero's Grave in central Altus Plateau. In the room with the giant falling blade traps, jump on top of the first one to ride it upwards, jump to the ledge on the left, and follow the path to a room with a pair of semi-transparent fog walls locked by an imp. Fit it before any fight where physical hits threaten to end the run.
name: Dragoncrest Shield Talisman +1

desc: Wrought iron talisman depicting a trio of ancient dragons. Vastly boosts physical damage negation. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Obtained from a corpse, in northern Crumbling Farum Azula. From Dragon Temple Altar, head north, down a drop off of a broken floor, down a staircase, through a window, down and across a floating chunk of floor, and right through a doorway to reach a long chain of floating debris. Halfway across...
whatItIs: Three dragons share this wrought-iron token, and it vastly boosts physical damage negation for as long as it is equipped. No activation, no upkeep.
whyItMatters: Soaking more physical damage turns the hardest hits a melee build can throw into survivable pressure, which is the core problem it solves. It comes from a family that has stronger and weaker versions, with each sibling absorbing a different amount.
whenToUse: The corpse sits in northern Crumbling Farum Azula. From Dragon Temple Altar, head north down a drop off a broken floor, down a staircase, through a window, and across a floating chunk of floor to a long chain of floating debris, with the corpse halfway across. Equip it in the heaviest melee encounters once this region of the game is reached.
name: Dragoncrest Shield Talisman +2

desc: A quaint bouquet of dried flowers, offered to a small grave. Raises attack power when a spirit you have summoned dies. The sorrow that flows from the untimely demise of a loved one is a tenderness shared by all, regardless of birthplace.
location: Loot: Belurat, Tower Settlement (Land of the Tower) Found in a small pavilion southeast of Belurat's Miquella's Cross. The path to it is hidden behind some rubble to the east of the entrance to the tower with the giant Spider Scorpions.
whatItIs: Dried flowers offered to a small grave, and the token raises attack power when a summoned spirit dies. The boost lands at the moment the spirit falls.
whyItMatters: Summoned spirits have a limited life, so turning their final moment into an attack spike gives a build a surge right when it needs to finish a fight. It suits spirit-summoning play that ends with a burst, and it is a niche fit for styles that never summon.
whenToUse: This one belongs to the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Look in a small pavilion southeast of Belurat's Miquella's Cross in Belurat, Tower Settlement on the Land of the Tower. The path hides behind rubble east of the tower entrance where the giant Spider Scorpions gather.
name: Dried Bouquet
effect: Raises attack power when summoned spirit dies

desc: A charm depicting the crazed, cavorting dance of the divine beast conducted at the tower festival. Raises potency of storms. Divine beasts are messengers of the heavens, and their rage mirrors the tumult of the skies, of which storms are the pinnacle.
location: Trade the Remembrance of the Dancing Lion, dropped by the Divine Beast Dancing Lion, with Finger Reader Enia. Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).
whatItIs: Storms are the theme here: a depiction of a divine beast's wild festival dance that raises the potency of storms while equipped. It is passive and constant.
whyItMatters: Any build whose offense leans on storm power gets a free bump in damage, which helps a caster or a spell-oriented playstyle without spending a stat point. It is a niche slot that only pays off when storms are actually part of the damage plan.
whenToUse: Obtaining it needs the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion on hand. Trade the Remembrance of the Dancing Lion, dropped by the Divine Beast Dancing Lion, with Finger Reader Enia, or duplicate one with a Wandering Mausoleums. Only one can be obtained per playthrough by either method.
name: Enraged Divine Beast

desc: A talisman depicting a special blessing of the Erdtree. Slightly raises maximum HP, stamina, and equip load. It is said that when the Age of the Erdtree began, such blessings were personally bestowed upon their recipients by Queen Marika herself.
location: Obtained from an altar in Fringefolk Hero's Grave, in western Limgrave. This dungeon is accessed from Stranded Graveyard after inserting 2 Stonesword Keys into the nearby imp statue, to unlock the semi-transparent fog wall. Proceed down the ladder and across the poison pond, to reach a ramp,...
whatItIs: Blessing of the Erdtree, and it slightly raises maximum HP, stamina, and equip load while slotted. All three nudges are passive.
whyItMatters: Raising HP, stamina, and equip load at once is a broad cushion that helps a mixed build carry a heavier shield without losing HP or mobility. Its family includes both stronger and weaker versions.
whenToUse: The altar holding it sits in Fringefolk Hero's Grave in western Limgrave. Reach the dungeon from Stranded Graveyard by inserting 2 Stonesword Keys into the nearby imp statue to unlock the semi-transparent fog wall, then descend the ladder and cross the poison pond. Equip it early on a mixed build and hold it while shopping for build-defining tokens.
name: Erdtree's Favor
effect: Slightly raises maximum HP, stamina, and equip load

desc: A talisman depicting a special blessing of the Erdtree. Raises maximum HP, stamina, and equip load. It is said that when the Age of the Erdtree began, such blessings were personally bestowed upon their recipients by Queen Marika herself.
location: Obtained from a chest in Cathedral of the Forsaken, in the Leyndell, Royal Capital region. This chest is available after defeating Mohg, the Omen in this same room. The room can be reached from Forsaken Depths in Subterranean Shunning Grounds.
whatItIs: Erdtree blessing on a talisman, and it raises maximum HP, stamina, and equip load all at once while equipped. All three gains are passive.
whyItMatters: The trio of gains keeps a character healthier, more mobile, and able to carry more weight, which suits any build that has not fully committed to one direction. It belongs to a line of tokens with stronger and weaker versions, so a similar effect appears in other places too.
whenToUse: The chest is in Cathedral of the Forsaken in the Leyndell, Royal Capital region, and it opens up after defeating Mohg, the Omen in that same room. The room is reached from Forsaken Depths in the Subterranean Shunning Grounds. Equip it once that fight is behind, and it serves a mixed build well.
name: Erdtree's Favor +1
effect: Raises maximum HP, stamina, and equip load

desc: A talisman depicting a special blessing of the Erdtree. Greatly raises maximum HP, stamina, and equip load. It is said that when the Age of the Erdtree began, such blessings were personally bestowed upon their recipients by Queen Marika herself.
location: Loot: Leyndell, Ashen Capital Obtained from a corpse in Leyndell, Ashen Capital, which can only be accessed late-game, after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade. This area is only accessible when approaching from the Forbidden Lands. Head west into the capital from the Grand Lift of Rold, down...
whatItIs: The Erdtree's special blessing, greatly raising maximum HP, stamina, and equip load. It stays passive and constant for as long as it is slotted.
whyItMatters: All three stats rise at once: more HP, more stamina, and more room for heavier gear, which is a wide comfort spread for a build that wants every cushion. The line of this token has both stronger and weaker versions.
whenToUse: It waits on a corpse in Leyndell, Ashen Capital, an area that only opens late in the game after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade. Approach the capital from the Forbidden Lands, head west into it from the Grand Lift of Rold, and work toward the corpse. Equip it on a late-game build that wants maximum cushion on all three stats.
name: Erdtree's Favor +2
effect: Greatly raises maximum HP, stamina, and equip load

desc: A talisman bearing an icon that depicts a group of masked figures. Raises potency of incantations. The figures represent the flock at prayer, their firm belief in the intangible inspiring even the solitary founder of their religion. What is faith if not an affirmation?
location: Loot: Sellia Crystal Tunnel (Caelid) Obtained from a corpse in Sellia Crystal Tunnel. The corpse can be found off to the right side of the main path, guarded by two Pests.
whatItIs: Masked figures in prayer on a canvas talisman, and it raises the potency of Incantations while slotted. No casting is required from the wearer to keep it working.
whyItMatters: Stronger Incantations mean every spell lands harder, which is the whole goal of a caster build that invests in spell offense. It is a niche fit for pure physical builds, where no spell is ever fired.
whenToUse: The corpse is in Sellia Crystal Tunnel in Caelid, off to the right of the main path and guarded by two Pests. Collect it on a Caelid run and equip it on any caster that wants its Incantations to hit harder.
name: Faithful's Canvas Talisman

desc: A talisman fashioned from thin feathers that embody the aspects of various creatures. Said to have grown on the human body long ago. Improves backsteps but increases damage taken at all times. Hornsent view the Crucible as sacred for the refinement wrought through its evolutionary gifts. Most prominently, their tangled horns.
whatItIs: Thinner feathers than its kin, and it improves backsteps while increasing damage taken at all times. It stays active for the whole time it is slotted.
whyItMatters: A crisper backstep is a small but real dodge tool against fast lunges and pounces, which helps a build that backs off instead of rolling wide. The constant extra damage taken is the price, making it a niche pick for confident dodgers.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion must be owned before it is in play. Equip it when dodging by quick backsteps is the preferred rhythm, and pull it out before any fight where the constant extra damage taken would tip the balance.
name: Fine Crucible Feather Talisman

desc: A talisman carried by assassins who strike unseen. Patterned on a scorpion freshly shed of its exoskeleton, its claws seizing a heart that burns with fire. Raises fire attack power, but lowers damage negation.
location: Loot: Fort Laiedd (Mt. Gelmir) Obtained from a wooden catwalk, hanging on the outside of a rampart, atop Fort Laiedd in the western Mt. Gelmir region.
whatItIs: A scorpion-shaped talisman that raises the power of fire attacks while it sits in the talisman slot. The price is a drop in overall damage negation, so every hit taken lands a little harder.
whyItMatters: It solves one narrow problem: making flame hit harder. That suits a build that deals fire damage through spells or fire-infused weapon strikes. The weakness shows up when the enemy swings back, because general damage negation is lower while this is in the slot.
whenToUse: Equip it in fights where the boss deals little fire, and swap it out the moment the incoming damage gets heavy. It is looted from a wooden catwalk hanging on the outside of a rampart, atop Fort Laiedd in the western Mt. Gelmir region.
name: Fire Scorpion Charm
effect: Raises fire attack, but lowers damage negation

desc: Talisman depicting a red ancient dragon. Boosts fire damage negation. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Guaranteed drop: Groveside Cave (Limgrave) Obtained by defeating the Beastman of Farum Azula boss fight at the end of the cave.
whatItIs: A small talisman engraved with a red ancient dragon that reduces the fire damage taken while equipped. Several drakestone talismans share this design at different strengths.
whyItMatters: Flame is one of the damage types that can end a new build in a single wall of fire, and a dedicated reduction turns that wall into a survivable risk. It holds exactly one effect, so the cost is simply the slot it occupies.
whenToUse: Take the slot in fights against flame-throwing enemies and burning environments, and give it back the moment the damage type changes. It is a guaranteed drop from the Beastman of Farum Azula boss fight at the end of Groveside Cave in Limgrave.
name: Flamedrake Talisman

desc: Talisman depicting a duo of red ancient dragons. Greatly boosts fire damage negation. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Loot: Leyndell, Royal Capital Obtained from a corpse that lies on the ground along the path eastward, out of the capital, towards the Grand Lift of Rold.
whatItIs: The two-dragon design belongs to the same fire-guard family and reduces the fire damage that reaches the character while equipped. It sits in the talisman slot like the other family members.
whyItMatters: When flame attacks are the constant threat, a dedicated reduction keeps the HP bar from draining between dodges. It does exactly one job and nothing else: blunt the fire before it lands.
whenToUse: Equip it through the fire-heavy fights and remove it once the threat is no longer flame. It lies on a corpse along the path that leads east out of Leyndell, Royal Capital towards the Grand Lift of Rold.
name: Flamedrake Talisman +1

desc: Talisman depicting a trio of red ancient dragons. Vastly boosts fire damage negation. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Guaranteed drop: Dragonbarrow Cave (Greyoll's Dragonbarrow) Obtained after defeating the Beastman of Farum Azula duo at the end of the cave.
whatItIs: Carrying three red ancient dragons, this fire-guard talisman trims the fire damage that lands while it is equipped. It occupies the talisman slot and works for as long as it stays there.
whyItMatters: Against bosses that mix flame into many phases, the extra reduction buys the seconds needed to line up the next attack. It belongs to the fire-guard family, so a different-cut version may turn up elsewhere in a run.
whenToUse: Keep it equipped in the late-game flame fights and swap it out the moment a different damage type takes over. It is a guaranteed drop after defeating the Beastman of Farum Azula duo at the end of Dragonbarrow Cave in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow.
name: Flamedrake Talisman +2

desc: Talisman with a large depiction of a red ancient dragon. Boosts fire damage negation by the utmost. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Loot: Fort of Reprimand (Scadu Altus) Found inside of a chest within the fort. Entering through the front gate, go down the staircase in the back right corner. Continue through the doorway on the left side of the hallway and follow this path until you see two soldiers standing in front of a...
whatItIs: A large red-dragon talisman from the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion that cuts the fire damage taken by a very large amount. It works passively from the talisman slot.
whyItMatters: By the deep stages of a run, fire damage arrives in big waves, and a thick reduction turns those waves into manageable ticks. It stands alongside the other red-dragon talismans in the same family.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion gates access to this one. Equip it in the DLC fights where flame is the main threat, and rest it when the boss switches elements. It is found in a chest inside the Fort of Reprimand in Scadu Altus, through the front gate, down the staircase in the back right corner, then along the hallway past the doorway on the left until two soldiers are in sight.
name: Flamedrake Talisman +3
effect: Boosts fire damage negation by the utmost

desc: A talisman bearing an icon that depicts a mass of masked figures. Greatly raises potency of incantations. The figures represent the flock at prayer, their firm belief in the intangible inspiring even the solitary founder of their religion. What is faith if not an affirmation?
location: Drop: Sage Gowry Obtained from the dead body of Sage Gowry after completing Millicent's questline, either by assisting her and then killing him, or killing her, and then visiting him to find him already dead.
whatItIs: Stamped with a mass of masked figures at prayer, the icon greatly raises the potency of incantations while it is equipped. Nothing needs activating once the slot is filled.
whyItMatters: For a Faith build, spell power decides how fast the fight ends, and a flat boost means every incantation lands harder with no setup or upkeep. It is the straightforward companion for a caster whose whole toolkit is built on incantations.
whenToUse: Equip it the moment the build turns to Faith spells and keep it through the spell-heavy boss fights. It drops from the dead body of Sage Gowry after completing Millicent's questline, either by assisting her and then killing him, or by killing her and then visiting him to find him already dead.
name: Flock's Canvas Talisman
