desc: A small, clouded mirror that reflects an image of a golden figure. Makes the bearer take on the appearance of a Host of Fingers. One of the ritual implements created by the Tarnished to deceive invaders.
location: Purchased from the Twin Maiden Husks at the Roundtable Hold.
whatItIs: Clouded and small, this mirror makes the wearer take on the appearance of a Host of Fingers while it is equipped. It stays active for as long as the slot is held.
whyItMatters: It is a deception tool aimed at invaders: an opposing figure sees a golden silhouette instead of an ordinary foe, and that gap throws the first exchange off. For a character that gets invaded often, those stolen seconds are the whole value.
whenToUse: Equip it in the areas where invasions are expected and leave it fitted during online fights. It is purchased from the Twin Maiden Husks at the Roundtable Hold.
name: Furled Finger's Trick-Mirror
effect: Take on appearance of a Host of Fingers

desc: A legendary talisman depicting the Elden Lord Godfrey. Raises charge attack power of sorceries, incantations, and skills. Godfrey was a ferocious warrior. When he vowed to become a lord, he took the Beast Regent Serosh upon on his back to suppress the ceaseless lust for battle that raged within.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Altus Plateau Obtained from the Golden Lineage Evergaol in southern Altus Plateau, by defeating Godefroy the Grafted.
whatItIs: Depicting the Elden Lord Godfrey, the icon raises the power of charge attacks from sorceries, incantations, and skills. It applies to charged moves, not to the quick ones.
whyItMatters: Held-and-released spells and charged weapon skills are the big-payoff moves of many builds, and this makes exactly those moves hit harder. It rewards the patient style of waiting for the opening and then unleashing the full charge.
whenToUse: Equip it in the builds that lean on charged incantations or weapon skills, and set it aside when the fight is about quick, uncharged hits. It is a guaranteed drop from defeating Godefroy the Grafted in the Golden Lineage Evergaol in the southern Altus Plateau.
name: Godfrey Icon

desc: Sacred cloth of the Godskin Apostles, made from supple skin sewn together. Successive attacks restore HP. The Gloam-Eyed Queen cradles newborn apostles swaddled in this cloth. Soon they will grow to become the death of the gods.
location: Obtained from the Spiritcaller's Cave in northeastern Mountaintops of the Giants, by defeating all of the bosses at the end of the dungeon.
whatItIs: Sacred cloth of the Godskin Apostles that sits in the talisman slot. While it is there, successive attacks restore HP as they land.
whyItMatters: The build heals as it attacks, which turns long grinding duels into a favorable trade. It suits a style of rhythmic, continuous hitting rather than single heavy swings.
whenToUse: Equip it in the attritional fights where steady combos are possible, and remove it against enemies that punish every swing with a riposte. It comes from defeating all of the bosses at the end of the Spiritcaller's Cave in the northeastern Mountaintops of the Giants.
name: Godskin Swaddling Cloth

desc: A talisman facsimile of a scarab, the carrier of treasures and precious things. This Golden scarab increases the amount of runes obtained from defeating enemies.
location: Obtained by defeating the dual Cleanrot Knight in the Abandoned Cave in central Caelid. This cave can be reached by heading east of the Smoldering Wall, and using a large dead tree root to traverse a canyon.
whatItIs: Facsimile of a scarab in gold that increases the amount of runes obtained from defeated enemies while equipped. It pays out in the fight, not during travel.
whyItMatters: Runes buy upgrades and spells, so a higher yield shortens the grind between every level-up and every purchase. The bonus triggers when enemies die, so it goes unused during long exploration.
whenToUse: Equip it in the grinding stretches of a run and remove it when the priority is finishing a quest. It is obtained by defeating the dual Cleanrot Knight in the Abandoned Cave in central Caelid, reached by heading east of the Smoldering Wall and crossing a canyon on a large dead tree root.
name: Gold Scarab
effect: Increases runes obtained from defeated enemies

desc: A braid of golden hair, cut loose. Queen Marika's offering to the Grandmother. Boosts holy damage negation by the utmost. What was her prayer? Her wish, her confession? There is no one left to answer, and Marika never returned home again.
location: Loot: Shaman Village It can be found in the Shaman Village in front of the Grandmother in the trunk of a decayed tree on a hill.
whatItIs: Cut loose as an offering to the Grandmother, this braid of golden hair from the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion boosts holy damage negation by the utmost. It works passively from the slot.
whyItMatters: Holy damage hits hard in the later content, and a deep reduction keeps a build without heavy holy defense from losing the bar in a few seconds. It is niche for builds that face little holy damage, because the slot would go to waste.
whenToUse: Getting to it means having the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion installed. Equip it in the DLC fights against holy-heavy opponents and rest it when the damage type is not holy. It lies in the Shaman Village in front of the Grandmother, in the trunk of a decayed tree on a hill.
name: Golden Braid
effect: Boosts holy damage negation by the utmost

desc: A talisman depicting the first school of graven mages — a nightmare that would continue to haunt the academy. Greatly raises potency of sorceries. The primeval current is a forbidden tradition of glintstone sorcery. To those who cleave to its teachings, the act of collecting sorcerers to fashion them into the seeds of stars is but another path of scientific inquiry.
location: Loot: Albinauric Rise (Consecrated Snowfield) Obtained from a chest atop the Albinauric Rise.
whatItIs: Depicting the first school of graven mages, the design greatly raises the potency of sorceries while it is equipped. The boost is passive and lasts for as long as the talisman is fitted.
whyItMatters: For a sorcery build, spell power is the whole economy of damage, and a flat boost makes every bolt land harder with no setup or upkeep. It suits a caster whose entire plan is glintstone sorcery.
whenToUse: Equip it in the sorcery build from the first spell onward and leave it through the magic-heavy fights. It is looted from a chest atop the Albinauric Rise in the Consecrated Snowfield.
name: Graven-Mass Talisman

desc: A talisman depicting a school of graven mages, the nightmare of the academy. Raises potency of sorceries. The primeval current is a forbidden tradition of glintstone sorcery. To those who cleave to its teachings, the act of collecting sorcerers to fashion them into the seeds of stars is but another path of scientific inquiry.
location: Loot: Academy of Raya Lucaria (Liurnia of the Lakes) Obtained from a large pile of crystals in Raya Lucaria Academy. From the room west of the Debate Parlor, just before the fight with the Red Wolf of Radagon, look for an empty bookshelf on the north side of the room, which is an illusory wall....
whatItIs: The school-of-mages icon adorns the design, which raises the potency of sorceries while equipped. It is a passive boost with no activation.
whyItMatters: It solves the same problem as the Mass design: making every sorcery hit harder than the base spell power would allow. A caster in the first hours of a build can feel the difference in how fast an enemy's HP bar drops.
whenToUse: Equip it the moment sorcery becomes the main tool and keep it while the spell list is being assembled. It is hidden in a large pile of crystals in the Academy of Raya Lucaria in Liurnia of the Lakes, behind the empty bookshelf that forms an illusory wall in the room west of the Debate Parlor, just before the fight with the Red Wolf of Radagon.
name: Graven-School Talisman

desc: A charm that resembles a great jar overflowing with weaponry. Vastly boosts maximum equipment load. The great jar grants this talisman to their warriors. Carry as much as you can - grow big and strong.
location: Rewarded by the Great Jar, after defeating 3 Great Jar's Warriors, in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow. This area can only be approached from Deep Siofra Well. Speaking with the Great Jar will cause 3 duelist summon signs to appear on the ground. Defeat all 3 duelists in turn to be rewarded with the talisman.
whatItIs: Shaped like a great jar overflowing with weaponry, it vastly raises maximum equipment load while it is equipped. No activation is needed.
whyItMatters: Heavy weapons and thick armor are the answer for a build that wants to tank hits and hit back, but the equipment load cap usually says no. It is the bridge that lets a heavyweight build carry the big sword and the heavy plate at the same time.
whenToUse: Equip it in the tanky, slow builds where the equipment load keeps blocking the gear, and remove it when the load is no longer a problem. It is rewarded by the Great Jar in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow after defeating three Great Jar's Warriors, and the area is only reachable from the Deep Siofra Well.
name: Great-Jar's Arsenal

desc: Talisman depicting a knight holding a greatshield. Boosts guarding ability. The knights of Leyndell once modelled themselves after the Tree Sentinels. Their purpose is to protect that which deserves protection, and thus the shield always comes before the sword.
location: Loot: Altus Plateau Obtained from a chest, within a black carriage, east of Erdtree-Gazing Hill Site of Grace, in western Altus Plateau. The location is more precisely east southeast of Lux Ruins and almost straight north from the Grand Lift of Dectus.
whatItIs: With a knight and greatshield stamped into the design, guarding ability is boosted while it is equipped. It is a passive effect.
whyItMatters: A build that lives behind the shield wants every block to absorb more, and this is the slot that makes the guard itself do the work. It suits a defensive style that blocks and waits for the opening.
whenToUse: Equip it in the shield-first builds and the boss fights where blocking is the main survival tool, and set it aside once the threat is over. It is looted from a chest within a black carriage, east of Erdtree-Gazing Hill Site of Grace in western Altus Plateau, more precisely east southeast of Lux Ruins and almost straight north from the Grand Lift of Dectus.
name: Greatshield Talisman

desc: A talisman in the shape of a green turtle. Raises stamina recovery speed. Turtles are known as a nutritious ingredient, symbolic of inexhaustible power. However, those who hold turtles to be wise creatures consider the practice of eating their meat to be barbarous.
location: Loot: Summonwater Village (Limgrave) Obtained from a chest in the cellar of Summonwater Village, in northern Limgrave. The cellar is locked behind a semi-transparent fog wall that can be unlocked by inserting one Stonesword Key into the adjacent imp statue.
whatItIs: Shaped like a green turtle, it raises the speed at which stamina recovers while it is equipped. It works passively.
whyItMatters: Stamina gates every swing and dodge, and a faster refill means more actions in the middle of a combo. It is niche for builds that never run out of stamina, because the extra speed then goes unused.
whenToUse: Equip it in the fights that demand long, unbroken attack strings, and remove it when the stamina bar is rarely empty. It is looted from a chest in the cellar of Summonwater Village in northern Limgrave, behind a fog wall that opens when one Stonesword Key is inserted into the adjacent imp statue.
name: Green Turtle Talisman

desc: Talisman depicting a golden ancient dragon. Boosts holy damage negation. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Obtained from a corpse in Stranded Graveyard, in western Limgrave. This corpse can be seen from the beginning of the game, hanging from a cliff behind where the player wakes up after dying at the Chapel of Anticipation, but cannot be accessed from inside the cave. Instead, start from the Seaside...
whatItIs: Carrying the image of a golden ancient dragon, it boosts holy damage negation while equipped. It belongs to the golden-dragon family of holy-guard talismans.
whyItMatters: Holy damage is the type that hits hard in the late game, and a dedicated reduction keeps the HP bar steady through the long exchange. The whole job is to blunt the holy hits before they land, and the slot is the full price.
whenToUse: Equip it in the areas where holy damage leads the assault, and rest it once the enemy deals a different element. It is found on a corpse in Stranded Graveyard in western Limgrave, hanging from a cliff that is visible from the start of the game after dying at the Chapel of Anticipation.
name: Haligdrake Talisman

desc: Talisman depicting a duo of golden ancient dragons. Greatly boosts holy damage negation. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Obtained from a corpse in Leyndell Catacombs, in central Leyndell, Royal Capital. From the site of grace, head up the stairs to the southeast, hang a right, and ride the elevator up to reach a room with three phantom enemies. Dispel the illusory walls next to the stairs, and another illusory...
whatItIs: Its design carries a second golden dragon, and holy damage is reduced while the talisman is equipped. The reduction is passive.
whyItMatters: Against opponents that lean on holy damage, a dedicated reduction holds the line through the long exchange. It suits a build that has no other holy defense and needs the slot to carry that job.
whenToUse: Equip it in the fights where holy beams and holy spells are the main threat, and remove it once the damage type shifts. It is taken from a corpse in the Leyndell Catacombs in central Leyndell, Royal Capital, past the room with three phantom enemies and the illusory walls next to the stairs.
name: Haligdrake Talisman +1

desc: Talisman depicting a trio of golden ancient dragons. Vastly boosts holy damage negation. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Obtained from a corpse in southwestern Mohgwyn Palace. The corpse lies in a graveyard next to the blood lake, below Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum.
whatItIs: The icon holds three golden dragons, and the holy damage taken is reduced while it is equipped. The effect works passively.
whyItMatters: A build that lacks its own holy defense can still walk through holy-heavy fights with this in the slot. It is niche for a holy caster, whose damage output already solves most problems.
whenToUse: Equip it in the late-game holy fights and swap it out when the boss stops dealing holy damage. It is found on a corpse in southwestern Mohgwyn Palace, in a graveyard next to the blood lake, below Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum.
name: Haligdrake Talisman +2

desc: A talisman depicting a hammer and a knight. Enhances stamina-reducing attacks against a blocking opponent. Hammers are highly effective against shield-bearing foes, so much so that they are known as "knight-killers."
location: Drop: Stormhill (Limgrave) Obtained by defeating Recusant Henricus in northern Stormhill near the Limgrave Colosseum, north of Stormhill Shack. WARNING: Be aware that joining Henricus's faction, Volcano Manor, will permanently prevent him from invading unless that character starts a new Journey.
whatItIs: It shows a hammer beside a knight and enhances the stamina-reducing attacks made against a blocking opponent. The effect is passive while equipped.
whyItMatters: Shield-first opponents chip the attacker's stamina with every blocked hit, and the bonus sharpens exactly that chip. It suits a build that fights a lot of shield-bearers and needs the pressure to break their guard.
whenToUse: Equip it in the duels against shield-bearing enemies, and note that joining Henricus's faction, Volcano Manor, will permanently prevent him from invading unless that character starts a new Journey. It is dropped by defeating Recusant Henricus in northern Stormhill near the Limgrave Colosseum, north of Stormhill Shack.
name: Hammer Talisman

desc: A small, clouded mirror that reflects a flesh-and-blood figure. Makes the bearer take on the appearance of a summoned cooperator. One of the ritual implements created by the Tarnished to deceive invaders.
location: Purchased from the Twin Maiden Husks at the Roundtable Hold.
whatItIs: A small, clouded mirror that makes the bearer take on the appearance of a summoned cooperator. Nothing to activate or manage, it only changes how other characters see the one wearing it.
whyItMatters: In a multiplayer session it turns the host into a disguise, since invaders cannot tell the host apart from a friendly summon. It is a niche tool that serves only PvP moments, and a solo campaign build gets nothing from the slot.
whenToUse: Equip it during a multiplayer session, especially when hosting and expecting invaders to trust a cooperator's silhouette. Buy it from the Twin Maiden Husks at the Roundtable Hold.
name: Host's Trick-Mirror
effect: Take on appearance of a cooperator

desc: An accoutrement worn by the ancestral followers. Raises immunity. (Immunity governs resistance to poison and rot.) Said to be a budding horn. The ancestral followers believed that the horns of a long-lived beast continue to bud like antlers, over and over again, until the beast one day becomes an ancestral spirit.
location: Loot: Ainsel River Found on a corpse in an ant's nest in southwest Ainsel River, near Ainsel River Downstream.
whatItIs: Worn by the Ancestral Followers, this budding horn raises the Immunity stat for as long as it sits in a talisman slot. Immunity governs resistance to poison and rot, so the bonus applies only to those two afflictions.
whyItMatters: It solves a specific problem: poison and rot hitting too often during long fights, since a higher Immunity makes each affliction less likely to take hold. It is niche outside rot- and poison-heavy areas, where a different stat would serve better.
whenToUse: Equip it for zones with heavy poison or rot, or for bosses that apply those afflictions, then swap it out when the threat is clear. It is found on a corpse in an ant's nest in southwest Ainsel River, near Ainsel River Downstream.
name: Immunizing Horn Charm

desc: An accoutrement worn by the ancestral followers. Greatly raises immunity. (Immunity governs resistance to poison and rot.) Said to be a budding horn. The ancestral followers believed that the horns of a long-lived beast continue to bud like antlers, over and over again, until the beast one day becomes an ancestral spirit.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Lake of Rot (Ainsel River) Obtained by killing an Ancestral Follower around the Lake of Rot, southeast of Lake of Rot Shoreside.
whatItIs: The same budding horn with a greatly raised effect, still aimed at poison and rot resistance. A whole line of horn charms shares this same design at different strengths.
whyItMatters: It gives a bigger margin against the same two afflictions, which helps builds that keep triggering rot during long fights. A one-hit-kill build that dodges well may not need the extra buffer at all.
whenToUse: Swap it in when poison and rot pressure is heavy, then move it out once the fight is over. It drops guaranteed from an Ancestral Follower around the Lake of Rot, southeast of Lake of Rot Shoreside.
name: Immunizing Horn Charm +1

desc: Ceremonial accoutrement worn by hornsent. Vastly raises immunity. (Immunity governs resistance to poison and rot.) Horns are sublime artifacts to hornsent, and their presence confirms the belief that they are a chosen people. Only the repeated sprouting of fresh horns can create a tangled horn, which is viewed as an irrefutable symbol of primacy.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Belurat, Tower Settlement (Gravesite Plain) Received upon defeating the Ulcerated Tree Spirit in the sewer swamp of Belurat, Tower Settlement. The Well Depths Key is required to access this area.
whatItIs: A ceremonial horn ornament of the hornsent that raises Immunity by a vast amount. Like the rest of the family, it targets the resistances to poison and rot.
whyItMatters: A bigger Immunity pool turns constant rot hits into manageable chip damage during long fights. It is niche outside rot-heavy content, since the effect only matters while poison or rot is actually landing.
whenToUse: Equip it for rot-heavy encounters once the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is installed. It is received upon defeating the Ulcerated Tree Spirit in the sewer swamp of Belurat, Tower Settlement, and the Well Depths Key is required to access that area.
name: Immunizing Horn Charm +2

desc: A talisman depicting the exultation of pests. Raises attack power when poisoning or rot occurs in the vicinity. "Rot for the scarlet goddess. O scarlet blossoms, flourish in distant lands, and return to us, the unwanted children."
location: Obtained by defeating Kindred of Rot in Seethewater Cave in central Mt. Gelmir.
whatItIs: Depicting the exultation of pests, it boosts attack power whenever poisoning or rot flares up nearby. The bonus rides on affliction events, so a rot cloud on screen makes the following swings hit harder.
whyItMatters: It converts a defensive problem into offensive pressure, which suits rot and poison builds that keep afflictions on screen. Against clean physical builds that never trigger those states, the slot does nothing.
whenToUse: Equip it on a rot or poison build and take it into fights where afflictions will be present constantly. Defeat the Kindred of Rot in Seethewater Cave in central Mt. Gelmir to obtain it.
name: Kindred of Rot's Exultation
effect: Poisoning or rot in vicinity increases attack power

desc: Handicraft depicting a golden crossed-tree. One of the items conferred to the Needle Knights. Enhances dash attacks. Long ago, the Needle Knights were in service of Miquella, but now they are no more. Save for one.
location: Quest Reward: Highroad Cross (Scadu Altus) Received from talking to Needle Knight Leda, by the Highroad Cross site of grace after successfully assisting her in assassinating the vengeful Hornsent at Shadow Keep. The player must kill Hornsent in the co-invasion with Leda in order to acquire this...
whatItIs: A golden crossed-tree handicraft that enhances dash attacks while equipped. It strengthens the strikes that follow a dash, turning evasion into part of the damage plan.
whyItMatters: It rewards builds that move aggressively, since dodging and striking in the same motion now hits harder. It is niche for players who stand still and block, because they rarely trigger a dash attack.
whenToUse: Equip it on any mobile build for fast fights, and it requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. It comes from Needle Knight Leda by the Highroad Cross site of grace after assisting her in assassinating the vengeful Hornsent at Shadow Keep, which means killing the Hornsent in the co-invasion with her.
name: Lacerating Crossed-Tree

desc: A talisman depicting a lance and a knight. Enhances attacks while on horseback. Knights on horseback are deadly foes. They see all below from their lofty position, meeting little meaningful resistance as they charge ahead.
location: Obtained from the northeastern-most tip of Stormhill directly west of the Divine Tower of Limgrave.
whatItIs: Depicting a lance and a knight, it strengthens every attack made while on horseback. Foot combat is untouched, so its value rises and falls with how much fighting happens on the mount.
whyItMatters: Mounted charges already hit with speed and weight, and this pushes that advantage further for builds that fight from the saddle. It is niche for a pure foot build, which never sees the bonus.
whenToUse: Equip it whenever mounted combat is expected, such as against enemy knights on horseback. It is found on the northeastern-most tip of Stormhill, directly west of the Divine Tower of Limgrave.
name: Lance Talisman

desc: A talisman carried by assassins who strike unseen. Patterned on a scorpion freshly shed of its exoskeleton, its claws seizing a heart that sparks with lightning. Raises lightning attack power, but lowers damage negation.
location: Obtained from a corpse in Wyndham Catacombs in eastern Mt. Gelmir. Midway through the dungeon is a semi-transparent fog wall, which can be unlocked by inserting one Stonesword Key into the adjacent imp statue. The corpse is inside, behind a coffin.
whatItIs: Carried by assassins who strike unseen, this scorpion charm raises lightning attack power while lowering damage negation. Lightning-based weapons hit harder with it equipped, and the character takes more damage in return.
whyItMatters: It is a classic trade for lightning builds, buying more punch at the cost of survivability. A build that is already fragile may not want to give up any defense for the extra output.
whenToUse: Equip it for lightning-focused fights and take it off when defense matters more than raw output. It is on a corpse in Wyndham Catacombs in eastern Mt. Gelmir, behind a fog wall that one Stonesword Key unlocks in the imp statue midway through the dungeon.
name: Lightning Scorpion Charm
effect: Raises lightning attack, but lowers damage negation

desc: A brooch depicting Lacrima, the long-tailed cat. Grants immunity to fall damage, but does not prevent death from a high fall. Lacrima features in the fables of Raya Lucaria, in which she is described as a faerie cat who was fond of playing in the great bell tower.
location: Loot: Academy of Raya Lucaria (Liurnia of the Lakes) Obtained from a corpse at the bottom of the lift in the Academy. From the Schoolhouse Classroom Site of Grace, head back outside and ride the lift down to the bottom (jump off the lift to the platform, near the bottom, because falling off the...
whatItIs: Depicting the long-tailed cat Lacrima, this brooch grants immunity to fall damage from ordinary drops. It does not prevent death from a very high fall, so it softens stumbles rather than making cliff diving safe.
whyItMatters: It removes a small but constant annoyance: hard landings no longer chip health during exploration. It is cheap to keep equipped, though it does nothing in fights where falls are not a factor.
whenToUse: Equip it while exploring cliffs and lifts, and it can stay on for the convenience it offers. It is on a corpse at the bottom of the lift in the Academy of Raya Lucaria in Liurnia of the Lakes, reached by riding the lift down from the Schoolhouse Classroom Site of Grace.
name: Longtail Cat Talisman
effect: Grants immunity to fall damage, but does not prevent death from a high fall.

desc: A talisman depicting the exultation of the Lord of Blood. Raises attack power when blood loss occurs in the vicinity. "Render up your offerings of blood to your Lord. Drench my consort's chamber. Slake his cocoon's thirst. His awakening shall herald the dawn of our dynasty."
location: Drop: Leyndell Catacombs (Leyndell, Royal Capital) The Lord of Blood's Exultation is obtained by defeating the Esgar, Priest of Blood, in Leyndell Catacombs beneath Leyndell, Royal Capital.
whatItIs: Held in a talisman slot, it raises attack power whenever blood loss flares up nearby. The bonus rides on bleed procs, so the moment the bleed timer fires, the following attacks hit harder.
whyItMatters: It turns the bleed proc into an offensive window, so a bleed build can punish the tick with a strong combo. It is useless on builds that never apply blood loss.
whenToUse: Equip it on a blood loss build for fights where the bleed timer will be running often. Defeat Esgar, Priest of Blood in Leyndell Catacombs beneath Leyndell, Royal Capital to get it.
name: Lord of Blood's Exultation
effect: Blood loss in vicinity increases attack power

desc: A talisman carried by assassins who strike unseen. Patterned on a scorpion freshly shed of its exoskeleton, its claws seizing a heart that shimmers with magic. Raises magic attack power, but lowers damage negation.
location: Obtained from Preceptor Seluvis in northwestern Liurnia of the Lakes, after giving him the Amber Starlight as part of his questline. WARNING: this must be done before giving Ranni the Witch the Fingerslayer Blade as that ends Seluvis's questline prematurely.
whatItIs: An assassin's scorpion charm that raises magic attack power while lowering damage negation. Sorceries hit harder with it in the slot, and the character takes more damage in exchange.
whyItMatters: It suits Intelligence casters who can still survive the reduced defense while gaining extra spell punch. It is the wrong trade for a fragile build or one that uses magic only as a side tool.
whenToUse: Equip it for caster-focused fights, then swap it out when a fight demands maximum durability. Obtain it from Preceptor Seluvis in northwestern Liurnia of the Lakes after giving him the Amber Starlight, and do so before handing Ranni the Witch the Fingerslayer Blade, which ends his questline.
name: Magic Scorpion Charm
effect: Raises magic attack, but lowers damage negation

desc: An eye engraved with an Elden Rune. Said to be the seal of Queen Marika. Raises mind, intelligence, faith, arcane, but also increases damage taken. These seals represent the lifelong duty of those chosen by the gods.
location: Obtained from a corpse in northwestern Siofra River, at the base of a waterfall behind the Dragonkin Soldier boss fight arena.
whatItIs: An eye engraved with an Elden Rune that raises mind, intelligence, faith, and arcane while increasing the damage taken. It is a four-stat boost in one slot, paid for in survivability.
whyItMatters: It helps hybrid casters who mix sorceries and incantations, since every spell stat goes up at once. The increased damage taken is the price, so it suits a character that can still dodge and survive.
whenToUse: Equip it on a hybrid caster for spell-heavy fights, and keep it off a build that cannot afford extra incoming damage. It is on a corpse in northwestern Siofra River, at the base of a waterfall behind the Dragonkin Soldier boss fight arena.
name: Marika's Scarseal
effect: Raises attributes, but also increases damage taken

desc: This legendary talisman is an eye engraved with an Elden Rune, said to be the seal of Queen Marika. Greatly raises mind, intelligence, faith, and arcane, but also increases damage taken by a similar measure. Solemn duty weighs upon the one beholden; not unlike a gnawing curse from which there is no deliverance.
location: Obtained from a chalice in southeastern Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree. The chalice resides inside a room locked by a semi-transparent fog wall, which can be unlocked by inserting one Stonesword Key into the adjacent imp statue. From Elphael Inner Wall, head east to the courtyard once guarded...
whatItIs: The legendary version of the rune-eyed seal, said to be the seal of Queen Marika. It greatly raises mind, intelligence, faith, and arcane while also increasing the damage taken by a similar measure.
whyItMatters: It multiplies the output of every spellcasting stat, so a high-level hybrid caster feels it across the whole kit. The matching rise in damage taken rewards a build that can still take hits or outrun them.
whenToUse: A hybrid caster that can afford extra damage taken should wear it during fights built around repeated casting. The chalice sits in southeastern Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree; travel east from Elphael Inner Wall to the courtyard, place a Stonesword Key in the imp statue, and the fog wall opens to reveal the room.
name: Marika's Soreseal
effect: Greatly raises attributes, but also increases damage taken

desc: Part of the golden prosthesis used by Millicent. The hand is locked into a fist that once raised a sword aloft. Boosts dexterity and raises attack power with successive attacks. The despair of sweet betrayal transformed Millicent from a mere bud into a magnificent flower. And one day, she will be reborn - as a beautiful scarlet valkyrie.
location: Obtained from Millicent, after killing her, at almost any time after she equips the Valkyrie's Prosthesis given by the player. The first location where she can be killed, and drop the talisman, is the Windmill Heights site of grace at Dominula, Windmill Village.
whatItIs: Part of the golden prosthesis used by Millicent, this locked fist boosts dexterity and raises attack power with successive attacks. The more hits land in a row, the more the bonus grows.
whyItMatters: It is built for fast Dexterity builds that spam multi-hit moves, because every swing in a combo adds to the bonus. It carries a lot of weight, so a lightweight loadout may feel the cost of the effect.
whenToUse: Equip it on a fast Dexterity build for fights with long combo windows, and leave it off slow, heavy-hitting builds. Obtain it from Millicent after killing her, once she has equipped the Valkyrie's Prosthesis that was given to her; the first place she can be killed is the Windmill Heights site of grace at Dominula, Windmill Village.
name: Millicent's Prosthesis
effect: Boosts dexterity, raises attack power with successive attacks

desc: This legendary talisman is a treasure of Nokstella, the Eternal City. Increases memory slots. This talisman represents the lost black moon. The moon of Nokstella was the guide of countless stars.
location: Loot: Nokstella, Eternal City (Siofra River) Obtained from a chest, underneath the throne, in northwestern Nokstella, Eternal City.
whatItIs: Shaped like the lost black moon, this treasure of Nokstella, the Eternal City, increases the character's memory slots. More memory slots mean more spells can be held ready at once.
whyItMatters: It solves the caster problem of running out of spell slots before running out of FP. A spell-heavy build gets immediate value, while a melee build that holds no spells gets none.
whenToUse: Equip it on any spell-casting build as soon as it is found, and it stays useful as spell loadouts grow. It is in a chest underneath the throne in northwestern Nokstella, Eternal City.
name: Moon of Nokstella

desc: A vividly-colored accoutrement precious to the ancestral followers. Raises immunity, robustness, and focus. Said to be a budding horn. The ancestral followers believed that the horns of a long-lived beast continue to bud like antlers, over and over again, until the beast one day becomes an ancestral spirit.
location: Obtained from a corpse in Siofra River, which lies at the end of a broken bridge, leading to Nokron, Eternal City. This area can only be reached from a waygate at one of The Four Belfries, next to a message that reads "Night Sky Unceasing".
whatItIs: Precious to the Ancestral Followers, this vividly-colored necklace raises Robustness, Immunity, and Focus all at once. Stronger and weaker versions of the necklace also exist.
whyItMatters: It bundles three affliction resistances into one slot, which suits builds that want broad protection without spending several talismans. It is a generalist pick, so a specialist build may do better with a single-stat talisman.
whenToUse: Equip it for fights or zones with mixed affliction pressure, then swap it out when only one affliction matters. It is on a corpse in Siofra River at the end of a broken bridge leading to Nokron, Eternal City, reachable only from a waygate at one of The Four Belfries next to the message that reads Night Sky Unceasing.
name: Mottled Necklace

desc: A vividly-colored accoutrement precious to the ancestral followers. Greatly raises immunity, robustness, and focus. Said to be a budding horn. The ancestral followers believed that the horns of a long-lived beast continue to bud like antlers, over and over again, until the beast one day becomes an ancestral spirit.
location: Obtained from a corpse in Nokron, Eternal City, atop the pillars above Hallowhorn Grounds. Climb around the terrain on the left side of the ruins to reach the top of the pillars.
whatItIs: The mottled necklace again, with a greatly raised effect on Robustness, Immunity, and Focus. It is one member of a family that has stronger and weaker versions.
whyItMatters: It is a practical choice when a build faces several affliction types at once, since one slot now carries much broader defense. It is niche against a single heavy affliction, where a dedicated talisman does the same job more efficiently.
whenToUse: Equip it for boss fights or zones that mix poison, rot, bleed, and frostbite, then remove it once the threat is clear. It is on a corpse in Nokron, Eternal City, atop the pillars above Hallowhorn Grounds, reached by climbing the terrain on the left side of the ruins.
name: Mottled Necklace +1
effect: Greatly raises Robustness, Immunity, and Focus

desc: Vividly-colored ceremonial accoutrement worn by hornsent. Vastly raises immunity, robustness, and focus. Horns are sublime artifacts to hornsent, and their presence confirms the belief that they are a chosen people. Only the repeated sprouting of fresh horns can create a tangled horn, which is viewed as an irrefutable symbol of primacy.
location: Mottled Necklace +2 is at the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. After unlocking the spiritspring, use it to reach a previously inaccessible area. The talisman is looted at the top of a staircase.
whatItIs: Worn by the hornsent, this ceremonial mottled necklace vastly raises Immunity, Robustness, and Focus. Other stronger or weaker members of this family exist as well.
whyItMatters: It is a broad defense upgrade for builds that cannot pin down which affliction a fight will use, since all three resistances jump together. It is niche for one-afliction specialists, who find a cleaner tool elsewhere.
whenToUse: Equip it for mixed-afliction content, because that content is part of the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. The item is looted at the top of a staircase at the Ancient Ruins of Rauh, after unlocking the spiritspring to reach the area.
name: Mottled Necklace +2
effect: Raises Immunity, Robustness, and Focus by +100 each

desc: A legendary talisman depicting the ancient king whose seat lies at the heart of the storm beyond time. Extends the duration of sorceries and incantations. It is said that the ancient royal city of Farum Azula has been slowly crumbling since time immemorial.
location: Loot: Crumbling Farum Azula Obtained from a chest in Crumbling Farum Azula guarded by three Beastmen and an invading Recusant Bernahl. From Beside the Great Bridge, climb up to the bridge, and head north, down some stairs and eventually a ladder, to reach a long walkway, where the invasion...
whatItIs: Extending the duration of sorceries and incantations, this legendary talisman suits casters whose timed effects need to last longer. Buffs and curses simply run longer while it is equipped.
whyItMatters: It stretches every timed effect, so a short buff can cover a whole fight and a damaging curse keeps ticking. Caster and buff-heavy builds get the most from it, while a build with few timed spells sees little.
whenToUse: Equip it on spell builds for long fights where a timed effect needs to hold. It is in a chest in Crumbling Farum Azula guarded by three Beastmen and an invading Recusant Bernahl, reached from Beside the Great Bridge by climbing up to the bridge and heading north.
name: Old Lord's Talisman

desc: A talisman engraved with the lore of an outer god. Raises arcane. The clan, who lost everything in the great fires, peered upon the corpse of their ancestor, normally an act of sanctity, and saw in its shadow a twisted deity. The clan had suffered such torment that the horrible thing was taken as an object of worship.
location: Loot: Prospect Town (Gravesite Plain) It can be found inside a chest inside a small building.
whatItIs: Engraved with the lore of an outer god, it raises the Arcane stat while equipped. It is a simple stat boost with nothing to activate and no trade-off.
whyItMatters: It helps builds that lean on Arcane, since a higher stat strengthens blood loss and related effects. It is niche outside such builds, because a pure physical or pure caster loadout gets little from it.
whenToUse: Equip it on an Arcane-reliant build; the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is needed first. It is found inside a chest inside a small building in Prospect Town (Gravesite Plain).
name: Outer God Heirloom

desc: Talisman depicting a knight bearing a pearlescent greatshield. Boosts all non-physical damage negation while guarding. The nature and the potential of impurity surpassed the understanding of the knights, and so they were forced to prepare for all threats known or unknown.
location: Found inside a chest in a small camp of Messmer soldiers in the woods. Southwest of the Taylew's Ruined Forge Site of Grace.
whatItIs: Guarding raises how much non-physical damage a shield can block, and the bonus lives for exactly as long as the guard is held. It covers every kind of non-physical damage rather than a single element.
whyItMatters: Spell-heavy bosses and elemental attacks land far softer while a guard is up, which is the moment a shield-bearer wants the most help. Outside shield builds the slot sits idle, so it rewards a character that actually blocks.
whenToUse: It needs the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, and it suits a shield build facing magic or elemental foes. It waits in a chest inside a small camp of Messmer soldiers in the woods, southwest of the Taylew's Ruined Forge Site of Grace.
name: Pearl Shield Talisman
effect: Boosts all non-physical damage negation by 20% while guarding

desc: Talisman depicting a pearlescent ancient dragon. Boosts non-physical damage negation. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Obtained from a corpse on the north end of the western isolated platform in Crumbling Farum Azula. This area is only accessible via the waygate at the first of The Four Belfrys in western Liurnia of the Lakes, next to a message that reads "Crumbling Lands". After traveling through the waygate,...
whatItIs: A pearl-white dragon medallion that raises non-physical damage negation for the duration it occupies a talisman slot. No button to press and no condition to satisfy; the bonus just holds.
whyItMatters: It lets a thin build trade blows with fire, lightning, and magic attacks without melting, which matters most against the spell-heavy bosses that hit before a guard is even up. It is a base member of the line, and the line has stronger and weaker versions.
whenToUse: Equip it on any build that takes heavy magic or elemental damage and is still hunting for a better version of the line. It drops from a corpse on the north end of the western isolated platform in Crumbling Farum Azula, reached through the waygate at the first of The Four Belfrys in western Liurnia of the Lakes, next to the Crumbling Lands message.
name: Pearldrake Talisman

desc: Talisman depicting a duo of pearlescent ancient dragons. Greatly boosts non-physical damage negation. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Obtained from a chest in the cellar of Wyndham Ruins in central Mt. Gelmir. The cellar is locked behind a semi-transparent fog wall, which can be unlocked by inserting one Stonesword Key into the adjacent imp statue.
whatItIs: Twin dragons on the face of the talisman, and a bump in the non-physical damage negation over the plain one. It still weighs almost nothing and simply holds the bonus while equipped.
whyItMatters: Casters and other fragile builds get a slice of spell damage eaten before it reaches the health bar, so a fight that previously ended in one or two hits becomes a fight that can be guarded through. It belongs to the same line with stronger and weaker versions, so keep an eye out for the other tiers.
whenToUse: Swap it in once a Stonesword Key is in the inventory, because the cellar of Wyndham Ruins in central Mt. Gelmir is locked behind a semi-transparent fog wall that the key opens on the adjacent imp statue. It suits a shield-less caster build that needs a flat non-physical defense boost.
name: Pearldrake Talisman +1

desc: Talisman depicting a trio of pearlescent ancient dragons. Vastly boosts non-physical damage negation. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: :Obtained from a corpse in central Miquella's Haligtree. From Haligtree Town, head northwest to a ladder, climb it, and jump backwards across a gap, to a platform leading to the corpse, which lies at the base of a statue, guarded by a Misbegotten Warrior.
whatItIs: Three dragons line the face of this one, and the non-physical damage negation grows again over the twin-dragon version. It is a quiet slot-filler that simply holds the bonus.
whyItMatters: The extra negation is what turns a boss's fireball or magic beam from a health-bar wipe into manageable chip damage. The family has stronger and weaker versions of the same dragon effect, and this one suits builds that want more soak without chasing further.
whenToUse: Equip it after Haligtree content if a caster or a frail melee build is getting melted by magic hits. It lies on a corpse in central Miquella's Haligtree; from Haligtree Town, head northwest to a ladder, climb it, and jump backwards across a gap to a platform where the corpse sits at the base of a statue, guarded by a Misbegotten Warrior.
name: Pearldrake Talisman +2

desc: Talisman with a large depiction of a pearlescent ancient dragon. Boosts non-physical damage negation by the utmost. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: It can be found within Shadow Keep, Specimen Storehouse. You must progress until the seventh floor to pull the lever that moves the statues. Once you do this, return to the third floor and find the head of the statue to pull this item from its beard. One way to do this is to visit the...
whatItIs: A single large dragon on the face, and the non-physical damage negation lands at the level its description marks as the utmost. It sits in a line with stronger and weaker versions.
whyItMatters: For a build that leans on blocking or on spell resistance, the extra soak is the difference between surviving a fire breath and feeding it. It comes from the Shadow of the Erdtree side of the dragon line, so it also fits late-game content.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is required first, and the talisman is tucked into the beard of a statue head on the third floor of the Specimen Storehouse in Shadow Keep. Pull the lever on the seventh floor that moves the statues, then return to the third floor and pull the talisman out of the head's beard.
name: Pearldrake Talisman +3
effect: Boosts non-physical damage negation by the utmost

desc: A talisman depicting a set of perfume bottles. Raises potency of perfume items. There are gardens known only to the perfumers. Whether hidden on the fringes of the highlands, or obscured by shadows inside caves, the flowers blossom in secret, waiting to impart their scent.
location: Obtained from a chest in the cellar of Perfumer's Ruins, in southwestern Mt. Gelmir.
whatItIs: Bottle-themed and light, the medallion makes every perfume item drink harder while it is equipped. It touches just the consumables and nothing about weapons or stats.
whyItMatters: Perfumes are the build's quick pre-fight buffs, and a potency bump stretches their effect into the exact moments a boss fight starts, so a single drink covers a longer opening exchange. Outside builds that drink perfumes every fight, the slot sits idle.
whenToUse: Equip it on a build that opens fights with a buffed perfume and wants the effect to land stronger. It sits in a chest in the cellar of Perfumer's Ruins, in southwestern Mt. Gelmir.
name: Perfumer's Talisman

desc: An old glintstone blade that has been stained with blood. Reduces FP consumption of sorceries and incantations at the cost of maximum HP. The old sorcerers would slice open their hearts with these blades to imbue a primal glintstone with their soul, and thus did they die.
location: Loot: Stargazer's Ruins (Mountaintops of the Giants) Obtained from a chest in the cellar of Stargazer's Ruins. The cellar is locked by a seal, which can be dispelled by summoning the Spirit Jellyfish Ashes near the NPC jellyfish that speaks, near the center of the ruins. Note that the NPC...
whatItIs: An old, blood-stained blade that trades maximum HP for cheaper spellcasting, so every sorcery and incantation sips less FP while equipped. It is a pure swap: more room in the FP bar, less in the health bar.
whyItMatters: A caster that runs out of FP before it runs out of health gains a long spell chain from the trade, which matters in fights where one wrong cast would end the run. The HP cost is the tax, so fragile builds or melee-first characters should skip it.
whenToUse: Equip it on a committed spellcaster once a health buffer from Vigor or a healing medallion can cover the reduction. It waits in a chest in the cellar of Stargazer's Ruins in the Mountaintops of the Giants; the cellar is sealed, and the seal is dispelled by summoning the Spirit Jellyfish Ashes near the speaking NPC jellyfish near the center of the ruins.
name: Primal Glintstone Blade
effect: Spells consume less FP, but maximum HP is reduced

desc: A fetid, overgrown cyst taken from facial flesh. Greatly raises vitality. (Vitality governs resistance to the effects of Death.) It is said that this cyst came from the corrupted visage of one unable to die a true Death. Indeed, it comes from the Prince of Death, scion of the golden bough and First of the Dead among the demigods.
location: Obtained by killing a Runebear in Deeproot Depths, in a cave behind a waterfall, northeast of the Deeproot Depths site of grace.
whatItIs: Fleshy and overgrown, the cyst raises vitality, the stat that governs resistance to the effects of Death. Nothing to manage; the bonus holds for as long as the slot is filled.
whyItMatters: Vitality is the stat behind resistance to the effects of Death, so the bump decides how much of that buildup a boss can pile on before the effect triggers. For a melee build that trades hits through a long fight, that is the difference between surviving the exchange and a sudden death.
whenToUse: Equip it on a build that wants more bleed resistance and already takes plenty of Death buildup. It drops from a Runebear in Deeproot Depths, in a cave behind a waterfall, northeast of the Deeproot Depths site of grace.
name: Prince of Death's Cyst

desc: A fetid pustule taken from facial flesh. Raises vitality. (Vitality governs resistance to the effects of Death.) It is said that this pustule came from the visage of the Prince of Death, he who used to be called Godwyn. As First Dead of the demigods, it's said he's buried deep under the capital, at the Erdtree's roots.
location: Obtained from a corpse next to the giant root-like face underneath Stormveil Castle.
whatItIs: Pustule on facial flesh, and a quiet bump in vitality, the stat that decides how much Death buildup a build can take. It sits in the slot and does its job with no condition attached.
whyItMatters: More vitality means the Death status effect takes longer to trigger, buying a build extra safety against the enemies whose attacks carry it. The payoff is felt most on a build that spends long fights in direct exchanges with tough bosses.
whenToUse: Equip it on a melee build that bleeds itself and wants a little more room before Death hits. It lies on a corpse next to the giant root-like face underneath Stormveil Castle.
name: Prince of Death's Pustule

desc: A talisman engraved with a scene from a heroic tale. Raises dexterity. Though born into the accursed rot, when the young girl encountered her mentor and his flowing blade, she gained wings of unparalleled strength.
location: Quest reward: Caelid Obtained from Millicent in central Caelid, after giving her the Unalloyed Gold Needle and waiting for her to recover.
whatItIs: An heirloom engraved with a scene from a heroic tale that adds dexterity while it is equipped. No cost and no condition; the stat simply goes up.
whyItMatters: Dexterity is the scaling stat for many fast weapons, so a bump adds free damage to every swing of a Dexterity build. A Strength build gains nothing from it, so keep it in the inventory.
whenToUse: Equip it on a Dexterity build that is a point or two short of a weapon requirement, or that simply wants free damage. It is a quest reward from Millicent in central Caelid, delivered once she has the Unalloyed Gold Needle and has recovered.
name: Prosthesis-Wearer Heirloom

desc: A legendary talisman depicting the Elden Lord Radagon. Shortens the casting time of sorceries and incantations. As the husband of Rennala, the red-haired Radagon studied sorcery, and as the husband of Queen Marika, he studied incantations. Thus did the hero aspire to be complete.
location: Obtained from a chest in Raya Lucaria Academy in central Liurnia of the Lakes. From Debate Parlor, head out into the courtyard, and right around the building. Jump over a fence, climb a ladder, and jump through a broken window to reach an upper landing, where the chest resides.
whatItIs: An icon of Radagon that shortens the casting time of sorceries and incantations while equipped. A faster cast lands the spell sooner, which is what separates a clean interrupt from a telegraphed one.
whyItMatters: Casters live or die on cast speed, because a long cast is a window for a boss to land a free hit, and a shortened cast closes that window. A melee character gets no value from the cast-speed bump.
whenToUse: Equip it on a sorcery or incantation build as soon as spells are the main damage source. It is in a chest in Raya Lucaria Academy in central Liurnia of the Lakes; from Debate Parlor, head into the courtyard, right around the building, jump a fence, climb a ladder, and jump through a broken window to the upper landing where the chest sits.
name: Radagon Icon

desc: An eye engraved with an Elden Rune. Said to be the seal of King Consort Radagon. Raises vigor, endurance, strength, and dexterity, but also increases damage taken. These seals represent the lifelong duty of those chosen by the gods.
location: Drop: Weeping Evergaol (Weeping Peninsula) Dropped by the Ancient Hero of Zamor boss found in the evergaol, just northeast of the Fourth Church of Marika.
whatItIs: Radagon's eye-shaped seal that raises vigor, endurance, strength, and dexterity at once, with a damage-taken penalty as the price. The four-stat bump is what makes it a popular early grab.
whyItMatters: It is a catch-all stat booster for a low-level build that wants to feel stronger across the board, and the damage-taken tax is the cost of buying that strength. The trade pays off in forgiving fights and gets risky against bosses that one-shot.
whenToUse: Equip it on a fresh build that wants four stats at once, or when a weapon's stat requirements are just out of reach. It is dropped by the Ancient Hero of Zamor boss inside the Weeping Evergaol in the Weeping Peninsula, just northeast of the Fourth Church of Marika.
name: Radagon's Scarseal
effect:
+3 VIG, END, STR, DEX 
+10% damage taken

desc: This legendary talisman is an eye engraved with an Elden Rune, said to be the seal of King Consort Radagon. Greatly raises vigor, endurance, strength, dexterity, but also increases damage taken by a similar measure. Solemn duty weighs upon the one beholden; not unlike a gnawing curse from which there is no deliverance.
location: Loot: Fort Faroth (Greyoll's Dragonbarrow) Found among the rats in the barn, reached from the roof of the fort. From the entrance, climb up the ladder and drop down from the tower onto the fort's roof. Drop down the hole on the other side of the gallows and go left and forwards of the ladder,...
whatItIs: A legendary Radagon seal, still an eye engraved with an Elden Rune, that raises vigor, endurance, strength, and dexterity, with the damage-taken penalty growing to match. It is a raw-numbers pick for a build that wants more of everything and can absorb the tax.
whyItMatters: The four-stat lift is a real boost for a build that needs raw numbers to hit harder and stand firmer, and the damage-taken increase is the tax for that lift. It suits builds that trade a little survivability for raw power.
whenToUse: Equip it when a weapon's stat requirement is out of reach and a raw stat bump is needed. It lies among the rats in the barn at Fort Faroth in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow; from the entrance, climb the ladder, drop from the tower onto the roof, and go through the hole past the gallows to reach the barn.
name: Radagon's Soreseal
effect:
+5 VIG, END, STR, DEX 
+15% damage taken

desc: A talisman adorned with red feathers, once used in ancient death rituals. Raises attack power when HP is low. The heart sings when one draws close to death, and a glorious end awaits those who cling so tenaciously to life.
location: Obtained from a Deathbird in central Liurnia of the Lakes, which spawns at night, northeast of Scenic Isle.
whatItIs: Red feathers on the talisman, and a bump in attack power that shows up just while the health bar is low. It is a risk-reward slot: the bonus is live in the danger zone.
whyItMatters: Desperation builds and aggressive duelists get a damage spike in exactly the window where a fight is already leaning their way, so a last-stand trade can flip a losing fight. Cautious builds that fight at full health never see the bonus.
whenToUse: Equip it on a build that likes to fight at low health and can survive the risk. It drops from a Deathbird in central Liurnia of the Lakes, which spawns at night, northeast of Scenic Isle.
name: Red-Feathered Branchsword
effect: Raises attack power when HP is low

desc: Talisman featuring a gallant portrait of Rellana, the Twin Moon Knight. Enhances attacks executed after maintaining the same stance for a certain length of time. Engraved as a reminder of the unparalleled devotion of those who left their homelands to serve Rellana. "By your leave, we will accompany you wherever your lunar vessel takes you."
location: Found in: Castle Ensis Found just behind Moonrithyll, Carian Knight, lying on an altar.
whatItIs: Rellana's face on the medallion, and a bump in the strength of attacks made after holding the same stance for a while. It rewards a patient, deliberate rhythm rather than a frantic one.
whyItMatters: It suits a methodical playstyle that keeps a consistent rhythm and wants the follow-up hits to land harder. A wild, switching playstyle never lines up the condition, so the slot can go to something else.
whenToUse: Inside the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, it is found just behind Moonrithyll, Carian Knight, lying on an altar in Castle Ensis. Equip it on a rhythm-based build that holds a stance and commits to the follow-up.
name: Rellana's Cameo
effect: Enhances attacks executed after maintaining the same stance for an extended period

desc: Handicraft depicting a golden crossed-tree. One of the items conferred to the Needle Knights. Enhances attacks executed after rolling or backstepping. Long ago, the Needle Knights were in service of Miquella, but now they are no more. Save for one.
location: Quest Reward: Highroad Cross (Scadu Altus) Received from talking to Needle Knight Leda, by the Highroad Cross site of grace after successfully assisting her in assassinating Ansbach at Specimen Storehouse. The player must kill Ansbach in the co-invasion with Leda in order to acquire this item,...
whatItIs: Crossed in gold, the trinket of the Needle Knights boosts attacks executed right after a roll or a backstep. It turns a dodge into a setup for the next hit.
whyItMatters: A dodge-heavy build gains a damage window in the exact moment it is already moving, so the roll that saves a life also loads the follow-up attack. Tanky, standing-still builds that rarely move to dodge get little from it.
whenToUse: It is a Shadow of the Erdtree expansion item, and that expansion is required first. It is a quest reward from talking to Needle Knight Leda by the Highroad Cross site of grace in Scadu Altus, after assisting her in assassinating Ansbach at Specimen Storehouse, where Ansbach must be killed in the co-invasion with Leda.
name: Retaliatory Crossed-Tree
effect: Enhances attacks executed after rolling or backstepping

desc: A talisman patterned after shields used in ritual combat held to honor the Erdtree. Raises defense when HP is at maximum. The practice had died out by the age of King Consort Radagon, but remains of the arenas where ritual combat took place can still be found in every land.
location: Obtained from a corpse in Leyndell, Royal Capital, lying in front of the coliseum in the south end of the city.
whatItIs: Shield-patterned, and it raises defense while the health bar is full. The bonus switches off the moment a hit lands, which is what defines the whole contract.
whyItMatters: It is a full-health buffer that makes the opening exchange of a fight much safer, since the first boss combo is usually the hardest one to survive. A chipped bar voids the bonus, so it rewards a careful HP habit.
whenToUse: Equip it on a build that starts fights at full health and wants the opening seconds to land softly. It lies on a corpse in Leyndell, Royal Capital, in front of the coliseum in the south end of the city.
name: Ritual Shield Talisman
effect: Raises defense when HP is at maximum

desc: A talisman patterned after swords used in ritual combat held to honor the Erdtree. Raises attack power when HP is at maximum. The practice had died out by the age of King Consort Radagon, but remains of the arenas where ritual combat took place can still be found in every land.
location: Loot: Mt. Gelmir Obtained from a chest in the cellar of Lux Ruins, guarded by the Demi-Human Queen Gilika boss.
whatItIs: Sword-patterned, and it raises attack power during the time the health bar is full. The bonus is live just in the clean, unscathed state.
whyItMatters: It rewards a disciplined build that heals back to full before engaging and wants the first volley to hit as hard as possible. A brawling build with a chipped bar mostly sees the bonus sit idle.
whenToUse: Equip it on a build that fights from a full bar and can afford to retreat and heal. It is in a chest in the cellar of Lux Ruins on Mt. Gelmir, guarded by the Demi-Human Queen Gilika boss.
name: Ritual Sword Talisman
effect: Raises attack power when HP is at maximum

desc: A bronze medallion depicting a roaring giant. Enhances roars and breath attacks. In ancient times, the giants were mortal enemies of the Erdtree. Their bellowing roars desolated nature, triggered avalanches, and whipped up storms of flame.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Limgrave Tunnels (Limgrave) Obtained by defeating the Stonedigger Troll in Limgrave Tunnels in central Limgrave.
whatItIs: Bronze and roaring, the medallion of a giant enhances roars and breath attacks while it is equipped. It touches just those two move types, so a sword swing is unaffected.
whyItMatters: A breath-weapon or roaring build gets a strength boost on its signature moves, which is the whole point of the slot for those builds. A normal melee or caster gets no value from it.
whenToUse: Equip it on a build that uses a roar or a breath attack as a core move. It is a guaranteed drop from the Stonedigger Troll in Limgrave Tunnels in central Limgrave.
name: Roar Medallion

desc: A talisman depicting a raised prosthetic blade. An honor bestowed upon the valkyries who serve the Goddess of Rot. Greatly raises attack power with successive attacks. The four sisters were born in the Swamp of Aeonia, and came to the Haligtree under the aegis of Gowry. And yet, those buds were doomed to never blossom.
location: Obtained from Millicent after choosing to assist her in defeating her sisters, as part of her questline.
whatItIs: Prosthetic blade on the face, and a bump in attack power with successive attacks. It rewards a build that commits to a long, unbroken combo.
whyItMatters: Fast, multi-hit weapons get their follow-up strikes stronger, which is the shape a combo build wants. A slow, single-hit build never gets the succession going, so the slot can go elsewhere.
whenToUse: Equip it on a fast multi-hit build that chains swings without pausing. It is obtained from Millicent after choosing to assist her in defeating her sisters, as part of her questline.
name: Rotten Winged Sword Insignia
effect: Greatly raises attack power with successive attacks

desc: A talisman carried by assassins who strike unseen. Patterned on a scorpion freshly shed of its exoskeleton, its claws seizing a heart with a blessed glow. Raises holy attack power, but lowers damage negation.
location: Obtained by defeating Anastasia, Tarnished-Eater, who invades the player near the Smoldering Church in northwestern Caelid.
whatItIs: A talisman that raises holy attack power while lowering damage negation, trading some protection for a stronger holy swing. Nothing has to be activated once it is slotted.
whyItMatters: Holy builds live on that extra attack power, and an empowered spell or skill can close a fight faster because of it. The downside is real though, because every hit the character takes lands harder once damage negation drops.
whenToUse: Equip it on a holy-focused character whenever holy attacks lead the damage, and drop it the moment raw protection is needed. It is found by defeating Anastasia, Tarnished-Eater, who invades near the Smoldering Church in northwestern Caelid.
name: Sacred Scorpion Charm
effect: Raises holy attack, but lowers damage negation

desc: A talisman fashioned from a dried twig, so slender that it might snap at the slightest touch. Prevent rune loss upon death, but will be lost itself in exchange. Believed to be a twig pruned from the Erdtree long, long ago.
location: Purchased for 5,000 runes from Patches, in Murkwater Cave in northern Limgrave, then later in Volcano Manor in central Mt. Gelmir. Purchased for 3,000 runes each (up to 3) from the Isolated Merchant in southwestern Weeping Peninsula, in southwestern Limgrave. Obtained from a corpse in eastern...
whatItIs: A twig talisman that is lost on death in place of runes, so a fatal hit costs the trinket instead of the carried runes. The trinket goes away, and the runes stay put.
whyItMatters: Dying normally deletes the runes on the character, and that loss can set a low-level build back by hours. Spending one cheap trinket to keep the whole haul is a small price for keeping a run alive.
whenToUse: Buy it for 5,000 runes from Patches in Murkwater Cave in northern Limgrave, or take it later from Patches at Volcano Manor in central Mt. Gelmir, with the Isolated Merchant in southwestern Weeping Peninsula as a third source. Leave it slotted through risky areas and pull it out once the rune pile is safely banked.
name: Sacrificial Twig
effect: Will be lost on death in place of runes

desc: Disturbing likeness of a man whose eyes have been gouged out. The corners of his mouth are upturned in an almost flirtatious manner. Constantly attracts enemies' aggression. It is said that the man, named Shabriri, had his eyes gouged out as punishment for the crime of slander, and, with time, the blight of the flame of frenzy came to dwell in the empty sockets.
location: Obtained from a corpse in Frenzied Flame Village, in northeastern Liurnia of the Lakes. The corpse is found on the steps of a building. Can be chosen as a starting gift when creating a new character.
whatItIs: Sends nearby enemies straight at the character, constantly drawing their aggression the moment it sits in a slot. The pull works at all times, with no switch to turn it off.
whyItMatters: It is niche, because the pull never turns off and it drags danger into crowded corridors. When it is wanted, the pull funnels every nearby enemy onto the character and away from anything else worth protecting.
whenToUse: Keep it for a run that wants every enemy chasing the character, or grab it as a starting gift when creating a new character. Otherwise it lies on a corpse on the steps of a building in Frenzied Flame Village, in northeastern Liurnia of the Lakes.
name: Shabriri's Woe

desc: Shard of the late Alexander, a shattered warrior jar. Greatly boosts the attack power of skills. Scraps of stewed flesh cling to the shard, and tatters of ornaments can be seen mingled within the slime. Relics of a red-haired champion, it would seem.
location: Obtained from Iron Fist Alexander after completing his questline, by defeating him in northwestern Crumbling Farum Azula, and speaking to him.
whatItIs: Grants a great boost to the attack power of weapon skills while it sits in a talisman slot. Every skill activation lands with the extra strength while it is equipped.
whyItMatters: Builds that win fights with one well-timed skill feel the boost on every single activation, which compounds across a whole fight. Since the skill stays the character's heaviest tool, amplifying it changes how often a boss can be pressured.
whenToUse: Finish Iron Fist Alexander's questline, defeat him in northwestern Crumbling Farum Azula, and speak to him to receive it. Equip it on any skill-heavy build, since the payoff lands on every skill cast.
name: Shard of Alexander
effect: Greatly boosts the attack power of skills

desc: A talisman depicting an archer wielding a longbow. Boosts attack power of precision-aimed shots. The Albinauric archers were in a class of their own, and their deadly long-range specialists struck fear into the hearts of men.
location: Loot: Albinauric's Shack (Scaduview) Found inside the Albinauric's Shack east of the road between Commander Gaius's boss arena and the Scadutree Chalice.
whatItIs: Strengthens precision-aimed shots, so a crossbow bolt or an aimed long-range attack hits harder while it is equipped. Only the careful, slow-aimed attacks benefit from it.
whyItMatters: Aimed shots are the bread and butter of a crossbow or longbow build, and the extra power turns a grazing volley into a real threat at range. It solves the problem of a ranged build feeling soft up close.
whenToUse: It is gated by the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, so a base-game run will never see it. Loot it from the Albinauric's Shack (Scaduview), which sits east of the road between Commander Gaius's boss arena and the Scadutree Chalice.
name: Sharpshot Talisman
effect: Boosts attack power of precision-aimed shots

desc: Shattered linchpin stone. Raises potency of kicking and stomping skills. Linchpin stones are spiritual anchors said to hold the ground in place and quell the fury of earthquakes—when this one shattered, the surrounding town fell into the broken earth. One account claimed that the moon itself had come tumbling down.
location: From the Moorth Ruins Site of Grace head South-East through the big stony archway. You'll directly head towards a house ruin. You can go through the house's doorway, exit on the small roof, turn left and around the corner you'll find the talisman lying there on a corpse.
whatItIs: Feeds power into kicking and stomping weapon skills, so those heavy impacts land harder while it is slotted. A build centered on those moves feels the change in every single one.
whyItMatters: It is niche, because only builds whose signature moves are kicks and stomps ever feel it. For those builds the boost lands exactly where the damage already concentrates, turning a finisher into a punishing one.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion unlocks it, so a base game run never reaches it. From the Moorth Ruins Site of Grace, head South-East through the big stony archway, exit a house ruin onto its small roof, and turn left around the corner to find it on a corpse.
name: Shattered Stone Talisman
effect: Raises potency of kicking and stomping skills

desc: A talisman facsimile of a scarab, the carrier of treasures and precious things. This silver scarab enhances item discovery.
location: Obtained from a chest in the Hidden Path to the Haligtree, Forbidden Lands. From the large circular platform in the large central room, drop straight down from the broken railing to land on an invisible platform, and walk directly South to a small room. Dispel the illusory wall behind a Grave...
whatItIs: Raises item discovery, which nudges the odds in favor of finding extra loot from chests and enemies. It stays passive, quietly working in the background.
whyItMatters: Item discovery decides whether a chest also yields a talisman or a rarer reward, so it matters most on a first clear of a new area. It costs nothing but a slot.
whenToUse: Equip it while clearing an area for the first time, then swap it out once the loot has been collected. The copy on record waits in a chest in the Hidden Path to the Haligtree, Forbidden Lands, reached by dropping from a broken railing onto an invisible platform and walking straight South to a small room.
name: Silver Scarab

desc: A talisman depicting an ancient smithing hammer. Inscribed with a smithscript. Enhances weapon-throwing attacks. In ancient times, smithing was a divine act, and blacksmiths interpreted the script they perceived in the wrinkles of molten steel to imbue weapons with souls.
location: Found in: Ruined Forge of Starfall Past The talisman is looted from a corpse. The body is inside a room filled with Fire Blob enemies, on the upper-most level of the Ruined Forge of Starfall Past.
whatItIs: Enhances weapon-throwing attacks, so a hurled knife, axe, or dagger carries more punch than usual. Thrown weapons hit harder, and the build that hurls them reaps the benefit.
whyItMatters: Throwing builds lose a weapon forever with every throw, which makes each thrown attack precious. The extra punch stretches a stash of throwables and keeps the pressure on while something can still be picked back up.
whenToUse: It is gated behind the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, so the base game never carries it. It is looted from a corpse inside a room filled with Fire Blob enemies on the upper-most level of the Ruined Forge of Starfall Past.
name: Smithing Talisman

desc: A talisman depicting a spear and a soldier. Enhances the counterattacks that are unique to thrusting weapons. Spears are standard weapons for soldiers in the Lands Between. They made it possible to respond to a ferocious foe with an equally ferocious counterattack.
location: Loot: Lakeside Crystal Cave (Liurnia of the Lakes) Located in a chest guarded by a pack of Demi-humans. The chest can be found in a campsite found by following the path into the cave without dropping down, past two braziers through a smaller cave in the back.
whatItIs: Amplifies the counterattacks that are unique to thrusting weapons, rewarding a well-timed riposte. The boost only touches those special ripostes, not normal swings.
whyItMatters: Spears and polearms already punish a boss for attacking, and the amplified counter makes that punish hit harder still. It solves the gap where a thrusting build's counter feels underwhelming against armored enemies.
whenToUse: Equip it on any spear or polearm build the moment a riposte becomes the core of the rotation. It is looted from a chest in Lakeside Crystal Cave (Liurnia of the Lakes), guarded by a pack of Demi-humans at a campsite deep along the path into the cave.
name: Spear Talisman
effect: Enhances counterattacks unique to thrusting weapons

desc: Talisman depicting a blue ancient dragon. Boosts magic damage negation. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Guaranteed drop: Earthbore Cave (Weeping Peninsula) Obtained by defeating the Runebear boss fight at the end of the cave.
whatItIs: A blue dragon talisman that boosts magical damage negation while it sits in a slot. Incoming spells and magic hits simply deal less.
whyItMatters: Magic damage negation decides how much of a spell gets through, which matters most against caster enemies and magic-heavy bosses. It is part of a family with stronger and weaker versions, so the base tier is a fine first step.
whenToUse: It is a guaranteed drop from the Runebear boss at the end of Earthbore Cave in the Weeping Peninsula. Equip it whenever magic damage starts to chip the character, and swap in a family member with a bigger boost as they turn up.
name: Spelldrake Talisman

desc: Talisman depicting a duo of blue ancient dragons. Greatly boosts magic damage negation. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Loot: Sellia, Town of Sorcery (Caelid) Obtained from a chest in Sellia, Town of Sorcery. The chest can be found in a small alcove in the northwest section of town, which is locked behind a magical seal. This seal can be dispelled by lighting the flame in the southwest candle tower, within the town.
whatItIs: The twin-dragon version of that family, greatly boosting magical damage negation while equipped. The padding is noticeably thicker than the base member's.
whyItMatters: The larger boost lets a spell-heavy build take noticeably softer hits when a boss leans on magic. It covers the same problem as the base member with more padding, so it is a natural follow-up once found.
whenToUse: It waits in a chest in Sellia, Town of Sorcery (Caelid), hidden in a small alcove in the northwest section of town behind a magical seal. Lighting the flame in the southwest candle tower within the town dispels that seal.
name: Spelldrake Talisman +1

desc: Talisman depicting a trio of blue ancient dragons. Vastly boosts magic damage negation. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Loot: Hidden Path to the Haligtree Obtained from a corpse in the Hidden Path to the Haligtree. From the large circular platform in the large central room, drop straight down from the broken railing to land on an invisible platform. Walk directly north, and then turn directly west, when aligned...
whatItIs: Part of the same Spelldrake family with stronger and weaker versions, and this one vastly boosts magical damage negation. The padding here goes further still.
whyItMatters: Caster-heavy late-game pressure becomes easier to shrug off, since a large share of incoming spell damage is absorbed before it lands. For a caster or any build that cannot out-tough magic damage, it converts painful hits into manageable ones.
