whenToUse: It lies on a corpse in the Hidden Path to the Haligtree, reached by dropping from the broken railing onto an invisible platform, walking directly north, and then turning directly west. Equip it during the Haligtree section and trade it out once a bigger-boost family member is carried.
name: Spelldrake Talisman +2

desc: Talisman with a large depiction of a blue ancient dragon. Boosts magic damage negation by the utmost. The ancient dragons, who ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree, would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. And so it is that the shape of the dragon has become symbolic of all manner of protections.
location: Loot Castle Ensis (Gravesite Plain) It can be looted from a corpse near the Castle Front site of Grace. From the Castle Front site of Grace, If you go directly north you can drop off of the cliffside and then follow the path east which will lead you to the storeroom where the talisman is located.
whatItIs: Boosts magical damage negation heavily while it sits in a talisman slot. Spells and magic pressure lose much of their bite.
whyItMatters: It is a strong pick for a caster when spell damage starts to dominate the fight. Since the expansion gates its location, it is reserved for Shadow of the Erdtree characters.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is required before it can be picked up. From the Castle Front site of Grace in Castle Ensis (Gravesite Plain), drop off the cliffside heading directly north, follow the path east to a storeroom, and loot the corpse there.
name: Spelldrake Talisman +3
effect: Boosts magical damage negation by the utmost

desc: A talisman depicting a smiling St. Trina, a vision conjured deep within a certain man's heart. Raises attack power when sleep is triggered in the vicinity. Only I am allowed to know. Of your velvety sleep. Its sweetly gentle embrace. So please, smile—for me, and only me.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Stone Coffin Fissure Drops from Thiollier when he becomes a hostile invader NPC in the Garden of Deep Purple. WARNING: This Talisman only becomes available if the player advances Thiollier's questline; killing him prematurely before he becomes an invader will not cause the...
whatItIs: Triggers a boost to attack power whenever sleep is set off in the vicinity of the character. The reward kicks in around the character, not just on a direct hit.
whyItMatters: It rewards a sleep-based strategy by making the follow-up hits land harder after the enemy is put under. It only pays out when sleep is actually triggered nearby, so it suits builds that lean on that status effect.
whenToUse: It requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, and it drops from Thiollier once he becomes a hostile invader NPC in the Garden of Deep Purple. Advancing his questline is required, since killing him before that point keeps the drop from ever appearing.
name: St. Trina's Smile
effect: Sleep in the vicinity increases attack power

desc: An accoutrement worn by the ancestral followers. Raises robustness. (Robustness governs resistance to blood loss and frost.) Said to be a budding horn. The ancestral followers believe that the horns of a long-lived beast continue to bud like antlers, over and over again, until the beast one day becomes an ancestral spirit.
location: Obtained from a corpse in eastern Liurnia of the Lakes. From Mausoleum Compound, head north up an incline, then left, and proceed southwest to a large tall rock formation. Walk counterclockwise around this formation to find a hole in the formation, forming an archway over a small ledge. Drop...
whatItIs: Raises robustness, the stat that governs resistance to blood loss and frost. Bleed and frost both build up more slowly while it is worn.
whyItMatters: Blood loss and frost punish low robustness with fast buildup, and the raise stretches the window before either triggers. A bleed-heavy enemy or a frost-coated arena becomes a manageable fight instead of a countdown.
whenToUse: Equip it when a build is squishy to bleed or frost and nothing else is available, and upgrade to a family member with a bigger raise as they turn up. The base member lies on a corpse in eastern Liurnia of the Lakes, found by walking counterclockwise around a tall rock formation near Mausoleum Compound until an archway opens onto a ledge.
name: Stalwart Horn Charm

desc: An accoutrement worn by the ancestral followers. Greatly raises robustness. (Robustness governs resistance to blood loss and frost.) Said to be a budding horn. The ancestral followers believed that the horns of a long-lived beast continue to bud like antlers, over and over again, until the beast one day becomes an ancestral spirit.
location: Obtained from a corpse in southwestern Consecrated Snowfield, in western Mountaintops of the Giants. The corpse can be found laying over a log, between the two large dead trees east of the Yelough Anix Ruins, guarded by two Ancestral Followers.
whatItIs: Greatly raises robustness, pushing back blood loss and frost even further. Status buildup takes longer to reach the breaking point.
whyItMatters: The larger raise matters most against the worst bleed and frost enemies, where buildup happens in a single strike or two. A build that already runs high robustness feels the difference as survivable status exposure.
whenToUse: It is found on a corpse in southwestern Consecrated Snowfield, in western Mountaintops of the Giants, resting over a log between two large dead trees east of the Yelough Anix Ruins. Two Ancestral Followers guard the spot, so clear them first before taking the trinket.
name: Stalwart Horn Charm +1

desc: Ceremonial accoutrement worn by hornsent. Vastly raises robustness. (Robustness governs resistance to blood loss and frost.) Horns are sublime artifacts to hornsent, and their presence confirms the belief that they are a chosen people. Only the repeated sprouting of fresh horns can create a tangled horn, which is viewed as an irrefutable symbol of primacy.
location: Stalwart Horn Charm +2 is found at the Bonny Gaol. Jump down into a hole and then climb a ladder to the east after passing rats. The talisman is located in a room with jar innards.
whatItIs: Serves as a horn talisman that raises robustness by a large margin against blood loss and frost. Bleed and frost become much slower threats while it is worn.
whyItMatters: The large raise is the answer when a status buildup would otherwise end a fight in one hit. It covers the same ground as the rest of the family with noticeably more padding.
whenToUse: It is locked behind the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. From the Bonny Gaol, jump into a hole and climb the ladder to the east after passing the rats; the trinket sits in a room with jar innards.
name: Stalwart Horn Charm +2

desc: An accoutrement worn by the ancestral followers. Raises robustness. (Robustness governs resistance to blood loss and frost.) Said to be a budding horn. The ancestral followers believe that the horns of a long-lived beast continue to bud like antlers, over and over again, until the beast one day becomes an ancestral spirit.
location: Obtained from a corpse in eastern Liurnia of the Lakes. From Mausoleum Compound, head north up an incline, then left, and proceed southwest to a large tall rock formation. Walk counterclockwise around this formation to find a hole in the formation, forming an archway over a small ledge. Drop...
whatItIs: Raises robustness just like its single-horn family members, covering the same resistance to blood loss and frost. The effect mirrors the family instead of outpacing it.
whyItMatters: It exists for the same reason the family exists, to stretch the window before bleed or frost triggers. A character that already stacks other resistance sources can use it to fill an open gap.
whenToUse: Grab it from the corpse in eastern Liurnia of the Lakes, approached by heading north from Mausoleum Compound up an incline, turning left, and proceeding southwest to a tall rock formation. Equip it during bleed-heavy or frost-heavy stretches, then move on once a stronger family member is slotted.
name: Stalwart Horn Charms

desc: A talisman engraved with the legend of a queen. Raises intelligence. The young astrologer gazed at the night sky as she walked. She had always chased the stars every step of her journey. Then she met the full moon — and, in time, the astrologer became a queen.
location: Obtained from a corpse lying at the top of the Divine Tower of Liurnia, in eastern Liurnia of the Lakes.
whatItIs: Adds a small free bump to Intelligence for any build that leans on that stat. Casters feel it in every spell they cast.
whyItMatters: A free bump to Intelligence eases the early hours of a caster build, when every point of spell power is felt. It asks for no stats and costs only a slot.
whenToUse: Equip it on an Intelligence-focused build from the moment the stat becomes the engine of the character. It is found on a corpse lying at the top of the Divine Tower of Liurnia, in eastern Liurnia of the Lakes.
name: Stargazer Heirloom

desc: A talisman engraved with a scene from a heroic tale. Raises strength. The mightiest hero of the demigods confronted the falling stars alone—and thus did he crush them, his conquest sealing the very fate of the stars.
location: Loot: Fort Gael Obtained from a chest in Fort Gael, in western Caelid. The chest is located on the upper platform of the fort, underneath a canopy.
whatItIs: Adds a small free bump to Strength for any build that swings heavy weapons. Heavy swings carry the extra weight behind them.
whyItMatters: The raise makes a Strength build feel the difference on every swing, and it can be the push a heavy weapon needs to come online. The single ask is the talisman slot itself.
whenToUse: Equip it on a Strength-focused character whenever the stat is the engine of the damage. It is looted from a chest in Fort Gael, in western Caelid, sitting on the upper platform of the fort underneath a canopy.
name: Starscourge Heirloom

desc: A talisman engraved with a stern likeness of Praetor Rykard, master of Volcano Manor. Restores HP upon defeating enemies. When Rykard turned to heresy, taking by force became the rule. The gods themselves were no different, after all.
location: Obtained from Tanith in Volcano Manor in central Mt. Gelmir after completing the third assassination quest, by killing Juno Hoslow in northern Mountaintops of the Giants, near the Shack of the Lofty.
whatItIs: A medallion bearing the face of Praetor Rykard, master of Volcano Manor, that refunds HP each time an enemy falls. It sits passively in a talisman slot and asks for nothing in return.
whyItMatters: The passive healing turns attrition fights and long exploration stretches into less punishing experiences, since every small victory pays back health without consuming a flask. It suits builds that fight in groups of enemies rather than one-on-one duels, and it removes the need to pause at a grace after clearing a room.
whenToUse: Pick it up from Tanith in Volcano Manor in central Mt. Gelmir after finishing the third assassination quest, or kill Juno Hoslow in northern Mountaintops of the Giants near the Shack of the Lofty. Equip it during open-field exploration or when clearing areas packed with enemies, and swap it out once a dedicated healing talisman is no longer needed.
name: Taker's Cameo

desc: A giant mass of intermingling Crucible attributes. Reduces damage taken from critical hits and head shots and improves the effectiveness of rolling and backstepping, but also increases damage taken at all times. Rumored to have sprouted upon giants and is known as the "mother of Crucibles" in ancient tower lore.
location: Found in a treasure chest in the western Ancient Ruins. If you have the Ancient Ruins, Grand Stairway Site of Grace unlocked, start there and take the nearby lift down; then, enter the square passage towards the south by using Torrent's double jump, using the adjacent pile of rocks to gain...
whatItIs: Fused crucible attributes compressed into one slot, it bundles every crucible effect together while raising damage taken at all times. The penalty never lifts: incoming damage stays higher for as long as it is equipped.
whyItMatters: It solves the problem of needing multiple crucible defensive perks when only one talisman slot is open, trading a constant vulnerability increase for the combined benefit of the whole family. It is niche: a build that does not already rely on crucible effects will feel the permanent vulnerability without gaining enough defense to offset it.
whenToUse: Reaching the chest that holds it depends on the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. The chest sits in the western Ancient Ruins; start from the Ancient Ruins, Grand Stairway Site of Grace, take the nearby lift down, then enter the square passage towards the south by using Torrent's double jump off the adjacent pile of rocks. Equip it when a build already leans on crucible defensive perks and one slot must carry the whole package.
name: Talisman of All Crucibles
effect: Grants effects of all crucible talismans

desc: A talisman depicting Godfrey, first Elden lord, receiving the precious sap. Increases poise after using a flask of tears. The Lord accepted the sap stoically, without any sign of wavering. No wonder the Lord of the Erdtree casts a long shadow over the lands.
location: Obtained at the Shadow Keep beside the big golden tree.
whatItIs: Depicting Godfrey, first Elden lord, receiving the precious sap, it raises poise after drinking a Flask of Crimson Tears. The poise bonus only activates after the flask is used, so there is no effect until that moment.
whyItMatters: Poise is the stat that prevents an enemy hit from interrupting an attack animation, so gaining it right after a flask drink opens a short window where a two-handed swing or a spell channel will not be flinched. It pairs well with heavy builds that already carry a Flask of Crimson Tears in the off hand, and it is niche for lightweight or pure caster setups that never use the flask.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion gates it, and the drop sits at the Shadow Keep beside the big golden tree. Equip it when a two-handed greatsword build needs a short burst of unflinched swings right after drinking a Crimson Tear. Drop it if the loadout leans toward pure casting or light attacks, because the poise window only fires on flask use.
name: Talisman of Lord's Bestowal
effect: Increases poise after using a Flask of Crimson Tears

desc: Talisman depicting the dread dragon of the jagged peak, whose roars cause the peak's molten fury to boil and churn. Raises potency of magma. Bayle was the foul dragon's name — a terrible harbinger of destruction whose challenge to the ancient Dragonlord ended in grievous mutual injury.
location: Found inside the Elder's Hovel in Gravesite Plain.
whatItIs: Engraved with the likeness of Bayle, the dread dragon of the jagged peak, it raises the potency of magma on attacks. Magma is a damage status that builds over multiple hits before detonating for a burst.
whyItMatters: Boosting magma potency makes magma-scaling weapons and spells reach that detonation noticeably faster, which shortens the time between the first hit and the big payoff. It is niche: builds that do not use magma at all will see no benefit, and the light weight means it costs almost nothing to slot in while testing a magma weapon.
whenToUse: This is a Shadow of the Erdtree find, tucked inside the Elder's Hovel in Gravesite Plain. Slot it in whenever the loadout builds magma on hits, and pull it the instant a different status ailment takes over as the main damage source. It stays empty weight in a caster or bleed build.
name: Talisman of the Dread

desc: A talisman depicting a twinblade and a confessor. Enhances the final hit ending a chain of attacks. The twinblade technique is a tradition of the confessors, who closely guard the secret of how they preserve the momentum of their attacks. Thus is the final strike of their onslaught all the more deadly.
location: Loot: Castle Morne (Weeping Peninsula) From the Behind the Castle Site of Grace, head down the cliff and northwest to the western corner of the castle there will be a tower guarded by a Scaly Misbegotten. Climb the nearby ladder and circle the top of the tower to find a chest containing this item.
whatItIs: Shaped after the twinblade technique of the confessors, it enhances the final hit ending a chain of attacks. Chain attacks are the multi-hit combos that follow up on a basic swing.
whyItMatters: Amplifying the last hit means the payoff of a full combo lands harder without changing the rhythm of the attacks that led into it. It suits two-handed and dual-wield builds that commit to long attack chains, while single-hit or spell-casting setups get no benefit at all.
whenToUse: From the Behind the Castle Site of Grace, head down the cliff and northwest to the western corner of Castle Morne in the Weeping Peninsula, climb the ladder near a tower guarded by a Scaly Misbegotten, and circle the top to find a chest. Equip it on any build that relies on multi-hit chains, especially dual-wield or two-handed swings, and remove it for single-shot or magic builds.
name: Twinblade Talisman
effect: Enhances final hit of chain attacks

desc: A talisman engraved with the legend of the Two Fingers. Raises faith. Fingers cannot speak, yet these are eloquent. Persistently they wriggle, spelling out mysteries in the air. Thus did we gain the words. The words of our faith.
location: Loot: Purified Ruins Obtained from a chest in the cellar of Purified Ruins, southern Liurnia of the Lakes, just north-east of Stormveil Castle. The stairs to the cellar are covered by wooden planks, which must be rolled over to be broken.
whatItIs: An engraved medallion bearing the legend of the Two Fingers, it raises Faith by a small amount. The bonus is flat and does not scale with anything else.
whyItMatters: Faith gates access to incantations, Faith-scaling weapons, and some passive auras, so a bump in the stat can be the difference between meeting and missing a spell's requirement. It is useful in the early game before Faith is built up through leveling, and it becomes less valuable once a build has Faith high enough that the bonus no longer changes which spells are castable.
whenToUse: Break the wooden planks over the cellar stairs at the Purified Ruins in southern Liurnia of the Lakes, just north-east of Stormveil Castle, to find it in a chest. Equip it early on a Faith build to meet spell and weapon requirements, and retire it once leveling has closed the gap.
name: Two Fingers Heirloom

desc: A talisman depicting a warrior two-handing a sword. Enhances attacks with two-handed weapons. The horned warriors were fitting figureheads for the military might of the tower they kept watch over, their deft attacks slashing through any and all foes.
location: Loot: Temple Town Ruins (Ancient Ruins of Rauh) Found inside the highest structure. After the fight with the Horned Warrior, just continue up the stairs into the next room to find a chest with this item inside.
whatItIs: Marked with the image of a warrior two-handing a sword, it enhances attacks performed with both hands on a weapon. The bonus applies only while the weapon is held with two hands.
whyItMatters: Two-handing a weapon is how a build extracts extra damage from a single weapon without switching to a heavier one, and boosting that bonus makes the commitment pay off more. It is niche for one-handed or dual-wield setups, and it shines when a character has invested in Strength or Dexterity enough to two-hand a greatsword or great axe.
whenToUse: Unlocked through Shadow of the Erdtree content, and it waits in the highest structure of Temple Town Ruins (Ancient Ruins of Rauh). Walk past the Horned Warrior, keep climbing the stairs into the next room, and the chest holds it. Keep it equipped on any build that grips a blade with both hands and wants the extra punch without juggling another weapon.
name: Two-Handed Sword Talisman

desc: A talisman in the shape of a two-headed green turtle. Greatly raises stamina recovery speed. Turtles are known as a nutritious ingredient, symbolic of inexhaustible power. Two-headed turtles are a favorite subject in the land of the tower, due to the spiral shape of their intertwined necks.
location: Loot: Rivermouth Cave (Gravesite Plain) Found inside a cave beneath a waterfall guarded by enemies just east of Rivermouth Cave.
whatItIs: Carved in the shape of a two-headed green turtle, it greatly raises the speed at which stamina regenerates. The effect is passive and lasts for as long as it sits in the slot.
whyItMatters: Stamina governs every attack, dodge, and block, so a faster recovery means fewer punished whiffs and more room to press an advantage after a successful hit. It suits aggressive builds that swing often and rely on dodging, and it is less valuable on setups that block behind a shield or fight with slow, heavy weapons.
whenToUse: Shadow of the Erdtree is needed to reach it, and it hides in a cave beneath a waterfall just east of Rivermouth Cave in Gravesite Plain, guarded by a small pack of enemies. Equip it on a build that attacks and dodges at a high tempo and needs stamina to snap back between each action. Take it off if the playstyle shifts to slow, deliberate, single-strike combos.
name: Two-Headed Turtle Talisman

desc: A discus made of verdigris, the corroded metal known for its heft. Raises defense with higher equipment load. Great weight makes for great strength. The strength to protect others.
location: Verdigris Discus is located in the Ancient Ruins of Rauh, positioned before a giant statue of a goddess. This area may be accessed via the sending gate closest to the Highroad Cross site of grace on the Scadu Altus. The gate must be unlocked with an Imbued Sword Key. After passing through, walk...
whatItIs: Heavy and cast from corroded verdigris metal, it raises the character's defense in proportion to how much equipment load is carried. The heavier the armor, the more defense it contributes.
whyItMatters: It rewards the tanky playstyle where a character wears heavy armor and still moves freely, turning the usual trade-off between defense and mobility into a small bonus. It is niche for lightweight builds that stay in the green or yellow load bar, and it pays off most when a character is already carrying the heaviest armor set they can equip.
whenToUse: It lives in the Shadow of the Erdtree section of the Ancient Ruins of Rauh, set before a giant statue of a goddess. Reach it by taking the sending gate nearest the Highroad Cross site of grace on the Scadu Altus, unlocked with an Imbued Sword Key. Equip it on the heaviest armor build in the loadout to convert that extra weight into actual defense.
name: Verdigris Discus
effect: Raises defense with higher equipment load

desc: A medallion with viridian amber inlaid. Boosts maximum stamina. The Erdtree's old sap becomes amber, treasured as the most precious of jewels in the age of Godfrey, the first Elden Lord. A primordial life energy resides inside.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Tombsward Cave (Weeping Peninsula) Obtained by defeating Miranda the Blighted Bloom in the Tombsward Cave.
whatItIs: A medallion with viridian amber inlaid that raises maximum stamina. This medallion has siblings at both a lesser and a greater strength.
whyItMatters: Stamina fuels every attack, dodge, and block, so a larger pool means more swings before a recovery window is needed and more dodges to escape a dangerous combo. It is the most universally useful stamina talisman for early-game builds that have not yet leveled Endurance high enough to feel comfortable.
whenToUse: Defeat Miranda the Blighted Bloom in Tombsward Cave on the Weeping Peninsula to claim it as a guaranteed drop. Equip it from the start on any build that swings or dodges often, and hold onto it until a stronger version from the same family turns up or a different stat becomes the bottleneck.
name: Viridian Amber Medallion

desc: A medallion with viridian amber inlaid. Greatly boosts maximum stamina. The Erdtree's old sap becomes amber, treasured as the most precious of jewels in the age of Godfrey, the first Elden Lord. A primordial life energy resides inside.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Capital Outskirts (Altus Plateau) Obtained by defeating Margit the Fell Omen in northwestern Altus Plateau, south of the Outer Wall Battleground grace. He will break disguise as a Commoner when you approach him. The decoy will still be there even if Morgott, the Omen King has...
whatItIs: Inlaid with viridian amber of a larger cut, it raises maximum stamina. Stronger and weaker members of the same family also exist.
whyItMatters: The extra stamina pool makes the difference between two consecutive dodges and one, which matters in any fight where a boss combo leaves a narrow window to escape. It is a clear upgrade over the base medallion for builds that still find themselves running dry mid-combo, and it becomes less critical once Endurance leveling has closed the gap.
whenToUse: Defeat Margit the Fell Omen in northwestern Altus Plateau, south of the Outer Wall Battleground grace, to claim it as a guaranteed drop; he breaks disguise as a Commoner when approached. Equip it as soon as it is available on any build that dodges frequently, and keep it until a different priority claims the slot.
name: Viridian Amber Medallion +1

desc: A medallion with viridian amber inlaid. Vastly boosts maximum stamina. The Erdtree's old sap becomes amber, treasured as the most precious of jewels in the age of Godfrey, the first Elden Lord. A primordial life energy resides inside.
location: Loot: Miquella's Haligtree Obtained from a chest in Miquella's Haligtree. From Haligtree Town Plaza head southeast, drop down to the rooftops guarded by Spiritcalling Snails, and continue southeast to perform a running jump across to another rooftop, which is slightly lower in height. Turn...
whatItIs: Set with viridian amber of a still larger cut, it raises maximum stamina. The family it belongs to includes both stronger and weaker members.
whyItMatters: The expanded stamina pool turns a fight that once required careful spacing into one where pressure can be maintained through a full boss combo. It suits mid-to-late game builds that have the stats to back up the aggression, and it is overkill on a low-level character who will not swing enough to need the extra buffer.
whenToUse: It is obtained from a chest in Miquella's Haligtree; from Haligtree Town Plaza head southeast, drop down to the rooftops guarded by Spiritcalling Snails, and continue southeast to perform a running jump across to a lower rooftop. Equip it on a build that already swings hard and dodges often and wants the stamina buffer to back up the aggression.
name: Viridian Amber Medallion +2

desc: A medallion with viridian amber inlaid. Boosts maximum stamina by the utmost. 'The Erdtree's old sap becomes amber, treasured as the most precious of jewels in the age of Godfrey, the first Elden Lord. A primordial life energy resides inside.' These medallions, of the largest variety, were conferred to Godwyn's inner circle of distinguished golden knights.
location: It can be found in Darklight Catacombs, right after the first canon imp. Jump over on the ledge to the right and then drop down to that small archway under it.
whatItIs: Polished and set with a generous inclusion of viridian amber, it raises maximum stamina. Other members of this family come in both stronger and weaker forms.
whyItMatters: The stamina boost is substantial enough that a build can chain through an entire boss phase without pausing to recover. It suits high-aggression setups that have outgrown earlier versions of the medallion, and it is overkill on a character who mostly blocks or casts spells.
whenToUse: Requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. In Darklight Catacombs, look just past the canon imp, hop onto the ledge to its right, and drop through the small archway beneath to find the medallion. A rolling or backstep-heavy build that wants to chain more attacks before stamina drains is a natural fit.
name: Viridian Amber Medallion +3

desc: Shard of a shattered warrior jar. Boosts the attack power of skills. Scraps of stewed flesh cling to the shard, and tatters of ornaments can be seen mingled within the slime. Relics of ancient royal warriors, perhaps.
location: Obtained by killing Iron Fist Alexander, before completing his questline.
whatItIs: Broken from a warrior jar, the shard boosts the attack power of weapon skills. The bonus applies to the special attack a weapon performs when its skill is activated.
whyItMatters: Weapon skills are the special attacks that consume stamina and often deal a burst of damage or apply a status, so boosting their power makes the risk of committing to a skill pay off more reliably. It suits builds that rely on a single skill as their primary damage source, and it is useless on setups that only use basic swings or pure magic.
whenToUse: Kill Iron Fist Alexander before completing his questline to obtain it. Equip it on a build whose main damage button is a weapon skill, and remove it the moment a different damage source takes over the rotation.
name: Warrior Jar Shard
effect: Boosts the attack power of skills

desc: A talisman depicting a raised prosthetic blade. An honor bestowed upon the knights who fought alongside Malenia the Severed. Raises attack power with successive attacks. The wings symbolize Malenia and her undefeated prowess. Though she never knew relief from the accursed rot she was born into, her blade was forever beautiful - and relentless.
location: Guaranteed drop: Stillwater Cave (Liurnia of the Lakes) Dropped by the Cleanrot Knight boss found at the bottom of Stillwater Cave.
whatItIs: Depicting a raised prosthetic blade, an honor bestowed on the knights who fought alongside Malenia the Severed, it raises attack power with successive attacks. The bonus climbs with each consecutive hit in a string.
whyItMatters: Successive attack scaling means each swing in a string deals more damage than the one before it, so the talisman amplifies exactly the kind of pressure that keeps a boss on the back foot. It suits dual-wield and two-handed builds that maintain long attack strings, and it is wasted on a build that spaces out single hits or relies on spells.
whenToUse: Dropped as a guaranteed item by the Cleanrot Knight boss at the bottom of Stillwater Cave in Liurnia of the Lakes. Equip it on a Dexterity or Strength build that chains multiple hits and wants the damage curve to climb through a full combo, and swap it out for a different talisman once the build shifts to a slower, single-hit tempo.
name: Winged Sword Insignia
effect: Raises attack power with successive attacks
